cards.definition: A slaughterhouse.
A book containing the alphabet, a primer. (n.)(adj.) abecedarian (n.),(adj.).
In low repute; lacking courage; despicable, self-abasing. Brought low in position, condition, or status. An outcast; a degraded person.
To renounce, repudiate or retract, esp. with formal solemnity; recant. To renounce or give up under oath; forswear. To avoid or shun.

Designating, being in, or pertaining to a case in Latin and other languages expressing direction from a place, or time, and variously also the source, cause, instrument and agent, manner, and sometimes place and time of an action or event. Of or pertaining to taking away or removing. Producing, removed by, or pertaining to surgical removal or wasting by melting (ablation).
To refuse or deny oneself some rights, conveniences, etc.; reject, renounce. To relinquish; give up. -gated, -gating, -gator
Sparing, moderate, not self-indulgent, esp. in food and drink. (-ly, -ness)
Hidden; secret. Difficult to conceive of or apprehend; recondite. (-ly, -ness, -ity, -ive)

A poem or other composition in which the initial (single acrostic), initial and final (double acrostic), or initial, middle, and finale (triple acrostic) letters of the lines make words. The beginning or end of a verse (arch.). A poem in which the consecutive lines or verses begin with the successive letters of the alphabet. Of the nature of an acrostic.
A musical piece or movement, or dance or ballet movement, in slow time.

Made of, or having the qualities of, adamant; impregnable, unshakeable. adamant - An alleged rock or mineral, to which many (often contradictory) properties have been attributed; formerly sometimes identified with the diamond or with the lodestone or magnet. Now only poet. as an embodiment of impregnable hardness.
Making no difference, non-essential, neutral. adiaphanous: not translucent, opaque.
Of or pertaining to animal fat. Of tissue: concerned with the storage of fat. adiposity - obesity, fatness. adipous = adipose.
In Greek mythology, a king of Pherae in Thessaly, and one of the Argonauts who took part in the Calydonian Boar Hunt; famed for his hospitality and justice.
Shade (a sketch) and so complete it. rare. Represent in outline, give a faint indication of. Shadow forth, typify, foreshadow, prefigure. Overshadow; obscure.
(also aerugo) The rust of copper or brass, verdigris, occ. the rust of metals generally.
A person who makes an affidavit.

A hard semi-transparent variegated chalcedony, having colors usu. arranged in bands. A diminutive figure (from those cut in agates for seals) only in sb. Ruby type (typography). A colored toy marble resembling an agate.
Soviet Communist propaganda, the system or activity of disseminating this.

(In ancient Greece) a contest in which prizes were awarded in any of a number of events, as athletics, drama, music, poetry, and painting. (In ancient Greek drama) formalized debate or argumentation, esp. in comedy, usually following the paragon, preceded by proagon. Conflict, esp. between protagonist and antagonist. (agones) (agonistic)

A malarial fever characterized by regularly returning paroxysms, marked by successive cold, hot and sweating fits. A fit of fever or shivering or shaking chills, accompanied by malaise, pains in the bones and joints, etc. Chill.
The wash of water against the shore or a river-bank. A deposit of clay, silt, sand, etc., left by flowing water, as in a river valley or delta.

An official distributor of alms on behalf of an individual, as a monarch, or an institution, as a religious house. A social worker attached to a hospital (no longer an official position). An alms-giver.
A person who writes from dictation or copies manuscript; a literary assistant. amanuense (v.).
Of or pertaining to a lover, lovemaking, or sexual love generally. amatorial, amatorious.
An odoriferous pale grey waxlike substance, which originates as a secretion in the intestines of the sperm whale and is found floating in tropical seas.
The scope, extent or bounds of something. Circumference, circuit. Boundary, limit. A sphere of operation or influence, range, scope.
Chiefly in 'all amort'. As dead, lifeless, inanimate, spiritless, dejected.
Self-esteem, self-respect.
A Greek or Roman two-handled vessel. A Greek or Roman liquid measure of varying capacity. amphoric: suggestive of the sound made by blowing across the mouth of an amphora. amphoral (adj.).

Orig. denoting a person whose choice of a love-object is governed by the dependence of the libido on another instinct, as hunger. Now: relating to or characterized by a strong emotional dependence on another or others.
A sentence or construction lacking grammatical sequence (also anacoluthia). anacoluthic (adj.).

(or Anapaest)- In prosody, a metrical foot consisting of the short or unstressed syllables followed by one long or stressed one. Opposite of dactyl, one long or stressed syllable followed by two short or unstressed ones.
A moderately slow movement or piece.
A metal stand for supporting burning wood on a hearth etc.; a firedog.

Any of various plants of the buttercup family, having petallike sepals and including several wild species with white flowers as well as others cultivated for their showy flowers in a variety of colors.
Strong dislike or enmity, hostile attitude, animosity. Purpose; intention; animating spirit. (Jungian psychology) the masculine principle, esp. as present in women.
Of the time before the Great Flood described in Genesis. Utterly out of date; very antiquated. A person who lived before the Flood; a very old or out-of-date person.
A gem described by Pliny, supposedly hydrophane. A hard, non-bituminous kind of coal consisting of relatively pure carbon. The dark grey color of this coal. anthracistic

In traditional Western Christian liturgy: a short sentence sung or recited before or after a psalm or canticle, a musical setting of this. A versicle or sentence sung by one choir in response to another. A response, rejoinder. antiphonary - a collection of antiphons. antiphony - opposition of sound, antiphonal.
Places diametrically opposite each other on the globe. Those who dwell there. (-e, -ean)
The loss of a previously held ability to speak or understand spoken or written language, due to disease or injury of the brain.
Loss or absence of voice through a defect in the vocal organs. aphonic - without voice or sound.
A summary, a conspectus; an insight, a revealing glimpse.

A person who abandons his or her religious faith or moral allegiance, a person who renounces religious vows without dispensation. A person who deserts his or her principles or allegiance; turncoat, renegade. Unfaithful to religious principles or moral allegiance, unbelieving, infidel. (sy, -tize)

(Also apanage) The provision made for the younger children of kings, princes, etc. (usu. a province, jurisdiction, or office). A natural accompaniment, a special attribute. A dependent territory or property. A perquisite.

Well put or applied, appropriate, suitable. Of a person: ready with apt remarks. Apposition: the placing of things side by side or in close proximity; the fact or condition of juxtaposition or parallelism. (-ly, -ness/tion)

Confirmation, proof. The action of formally or authoritatively declaring good or true; sanction, endorsement, approval or satisfaction expressed or felt. Approving expressly or formally. (approbate, approbatory)
Of, like, or containing water; watery. Rocks or sediments formed of matter deposited in or by water.

A sinuous, spiraling, undulating, or serpentine line or linear motif. A pose in ballet in which the dancer stands on one leg with one arm extended in front and the other leg and arm extended behind. A short, fanciful musical piece, typically for piano. An ornamental object in which flowers, foliage, fruits, vases, animals, and figures are represented in a fancifully combined pattern. (-ly)
The lowest part of an entablature, resting immediately upon the abacus on the capital of a column. The various parts surrounding a door or window. Molding around the exterior of an arch.

The chief magistrate, or, after the time of Solon, each of the nine chief magistrates of ancient Athens. Ruler, president. A power subordinate to God, held by some of the Gnostics to have created the world.
Silver coin; money, cash. The metal silver. Heraldry - silver or white.
A large merchant ship, esp. one with a rich cargo. A fleet of such ships. An opulent supply.

Armor. The protective covering of an animal or plant, or any part serving for defense or offense. The part of an electric machine that includes the main current-carrying winding and in which the electromotive force is induced, a pivot activated by magnet. In sculpture, a skeletal framework for clay or wax.

armilla - An ancient astronomical instrument consisting of a graduated ring or hoop, fixed in the plane of the equator, sometimes crossed by another in the plane of the meridian (solstitial armilla). Armillary sphere - hoops representing celestial circles. armillary - Of or pertaining to armillae.
The sounding of the notes of a chord in (usu. rapid upward) succession, not simultaneously; a chord so sounded.
Downright; thorough; unmitigated; notorious. Wandering; errant. Thoroughgoing; utter; confirmed; flagrant.

A rich tapestry, tapestry weave, wall hanging. A curtain suspended loosely across a stage and used as a backdrop or part of a stage setting. (used w/ a singular verb) a gift presented at marriage by a husband to his wife in consideration of her dowry.
A concealed thought or intention; an ulterior motive; a mental reservation.
An ambitious or self-seeking person. arrivism - The behavior or character of an arriviste.
Harshness or sharpness of temper, esp. as displayed in tone or manner; bitterness, acrimony. asperities - embittered feelings. asperate - make rough or harsh. asperous - rough, rugged, harsh, bitter.
A plant of the lily family native to the Mediterranean with white or yellow flowers. An immortal flower said to cover the Elysian fields.
A solemn affirmation, an emphatic declaration or confirmation; an oath.
Chief magician, a great wizard.
The superior of a large monastery in the Orthodox Church, also used as an honorary title of a monastic priest.

Resemblance or correspondence of sound between two syllables. The rhyming of one word with another in accented vowel and those that follow, but not in consonants, or (less usually) in consonants but not in vowels. Correspondence more or less incomplete. assonate: sound like a bell; correspond in sound.
Urbane irony; polite mockery.
Loss of strength, weakness.
Resemblance to more remote ancestors rather than to parents; tendency of animals or plants to revert to an ancestral type.
One of the three Moirae, the Greek goddesses of fate, who cuts the thread of life; identified with Roman Morta.
Cut into, pierce. Broach (a cask, etc). Attack, meddle with. Begin, undertake.
A fragrant volatile essence, esp. that obtained from rose-petals (attar of roses).

Make thin or slender. Make thin in consistency, dilute, rarefy. Weaken, reduce in force, effect, value, etc. Reduce the amplitude of (an oscillation, esp. an electrical signal). Become slender, weaker, etc.; decrease in amplitude. Slender, thin; emaciated; tapering to thinness (adj). Thin in consistency; weakened, rarefied, refined.

A Roman religious official who interpreted omens derived from the behavior of birds, the appearance of entrails, etc. and gave advice in accordance. Soothsayer, diviner, prophet. To usher (sometimes with 'in') with auguries; inaugurate. To take auguries, conjecture with signs, have a foreboding. Augury - augural rite or token. Divine, forebode, intimate, portend.
Any of several short-winged diving sea birds of the family Alcidae, native to the northern oceans, which includes razor-bills, guillemots, and puffins.
Of or pertaining to gold, golden, spec. of gold in the trivalent state. Aural, of pertaining to, or received by the ear. Ala, of or pertaining to an aura.
The extinct wild ox, which is the ancestor of domestic cattle in Europe and many parts of the world. Also the European bison.
Indigenous, native, aboriginal. Autochthon - an aboriginal. Also used in geology to describe native rocks.
Autonomous. Of or pertaining to the autonomic nervous system or under its control. (cellular biology) produced by internal forces or causes; spontaneous. (-al, -ally)
Stop! Cease! Hold! (nautical)

A brownish, ornamental glass containing sparkling particles of copper or another foreign material. A variant quartz of a reddish [illegible] with particles of another mineral (also mica or hematite, respectively).
Of, pertaining to, or resembling an uncle.
Free, in Romance, Persian, Urdu and Hindi.
A follower of Bacchus. A drunken reveller. An occasion of drunken revelry, orgy. bacchanalia/bacchant, bacchante, or votary of Bacchus. bacchant: drunken reveller, united to revelry.
A blow with something flat or soft. Beat, strike, strike (the ground) with the head of a golf club [illegible] yet enjoy a stroke.
A trifling [illegible]. A thing of little importance; a very easy task. A short, light musical piece.
A poem, usu. one of stanzas of 8 or 10 lines, last one being a refrain, and an envoi. A short, romantic musical composition, for piano. An extended or dramatic piece of music, usu. for [illegible].
A suburb of a large city. In France, an agglomeration (the suburbs (banlieue)) in which mainly French of foreign descent or foreign immigrants reside.
An ocean-going sailing vessel of practically any type. A fore-and-aft rigged vessel [illegible] and the other masts fully rigged. A (large) canoe, boat, any small sailing vessel.
Mountain, hill. Grave-mound or tumulus. A castrated pig. A handcart for carrying loads. [illegible].
A fabulous reptile, said to slay [illegible], hatched by a serpent from a cock's egg. A person who owns a look with a destructive or venomous power. A large, tropical American lizard.
Fibrous material from the phloem of plants, that is hemp, jute, or [illegible]. phloem - one of the two chief components of vascular tissue in plants, synthesized and downward from the leaves.
The [illegible] of a Khazar [illegible] with a bishop's spiritual leader. [illegible] the governor of [illegible].
Covered, hidden, involved in the darkness of [illegible]. Involved in intellectual or moral darkness; benighted, under a cloud. (benightment, -edness)

Benediction; an utterance of good wishes. A blessing, an appeal or expression of divine favour or the blessing, mercy. The ceremony by which things are set apart or consecrated [illegible]; a benediction.
The biogeographic region that includes the bottom of a lake, sea, or ocean, and the littoral and supralittoral zones of the shore. benthic division; benthonic zone.
Clothes made to individual order, custom-made; a bespoke jacket. Making or selling such clothes; a bespoke tailor.
The bane of someone's life, an insufferable person or thing; an object of aversion.
(Also byzant). A gold or silver coin orig. minted at Byzantium (later Constantinople), widely used in the currency of medieval Europe. (heraldry) A gold roundel representing such a coin.

The groove and projecting lip holding a gem, watch-glass, etc., the rim holding a cover of glass etc. The sloped edge of a chisel or other cutting tool. The oblique sides or faces of a cut gem. To grind or cut to a sloping edge.
A concretion (hardened nodule in the body) found in the stomach or intestines of certain animals (chiefly ruminants), formerly believed to be antidotal.
Plunder or spoil, make away with (the property of another). Consume (drink) to excess, guzzle, 'booze'.
A mild preparation of marijuana made from young leaves and stems of the Indian hemp plant, cannabis sativa, drunk with milk or water as a fermented brew or smoked for its hallucinogenic effects.
A person affected with or given to bibliomania, a passion for the collecting and possessing of books.
A slender sword having a blade of notable temper and elasticity. (also bilbo) An iron bar with sliding shackles for confining the ankles of prisoners.
A fish market in London noted for vituperative language. Scurrilous abuse, violent invective. A foul-mouthed person, a scold.
A girl, a woman. (Arabic slang)

Naturally-occurring asphalt from the Middle East, used as mortar, etc. Any natural or artificial black or brown solid or viscous liquid consisting largely of hydrocarbons. A pigment made from asphalt.
Kindly, clement, gentle. Joyous, merry, glad, happy, well pleased. Heedless, careless.

A dagger, a stiletto. A small pointed instrument for piercing cloth, etc. A long pin used to fasten up the hair. A person squeezed between two others. An instrument for removing pieces of printing type.
Bombe - a round or melon-shaped frozen mold made from a combination of ice creams, mousses, or ices. Bombé - curving or swelling outward, in furniture.

A leafy shelter or recess, arbor. Rustic dwelling, cottage. A lady's boudoir in a medieval castle. To enclose in or as in a bower; embrace. The anchor carried at a ship's bow. A musician who performs with a bow on a stringed instrument. Bowery - containing bowers, leafy, shady. Among Dutch NY'ers, a farm or country seat.
A worker in brass. A pan or stand for holding lighted coals as a portable heater.
Breechcloth; loincloth.
A Christian book containing the service for each day, to be recited by those in orders. In early use also, an abridged version of the psalms. A brief statement; a summary.

A person who engages in bricolage, the construction or creation from whatever is immediately available for use; something constructed or created in this way, an assemblage of haphazard or incongruous elements.
(from St. Bride's Well in London) a prison, a reformatory. A prison stood near the well.
A bandit, esp. one of a band of robbers in mountain or forest regions.
To voice abroad, rumor (followed by 'about' or 'abroad'); speak of, make famous. A noise or clamor. Rumor; report. Fame, reputation.

A fine linen or cotton fabric (obsolete). A coarse cloth stiffened with gum or paste. Stiffness of manner. men in buckram - non-existent persons, figments. Pad or stiffen, give a starched pomposity or illusory strength to.

A half-boot. A kind of thick-soled boot worn by tragic actors in the ancient Athenian theatre; fig. tragic drama, tragedy. (also cothurnus) sock and buskin - the theatrical profession; comedy and tragedy; drama.
A West Indian or S. American Indian native chief.
A register of property showing the extent, value, and ownership of land for taxation. Cadastral - Of or pertaining to a cadastre.
Cotton wool, floss silk, fluff, surgical lint. A tape or binding of worsted yarn, crewel; worsted material, coarse serge. The aquatic larva of a caddis-fly.
A travelling tinker; a Gypsy.
A pyramid of rough stones raised as a memorial or to mark a path, etc. (vt) Provide or mark with a cairn or cairns; pile as a cairn.
A large watertight chamber open at the bottom, from which the water is kept out by air pressure, used in laying foundations under water. A chest or wagon for ammunition.
A light, low-wheeled carriage with a removable folding hood. (from German)
A secret society akin to the Mafia operating in the Neapolitan district. Any organized body engaged in extortion or other dishonest activities.

Slope, slant, tilt; turn over or upside down, push or pitch sideways. Ephemeral catchwords; affected or insincere phraseology, esp. implying piety which does not exist. An oblique or slanting edge which cuts the corner off a square, cube, etc.
The outer or inner corner of the eye, where the lids meet.
An ornamented covering spread over a horse's saddle or harness, (usu. in pl.) a horse's trappings. A set of clothes or ornaments, an outfit. To put trappings or hangings on; deck.
Divination by smoke.

A castrated domestic cock (usu. one fattened for eating). A eunuch. A dull-witted person. A billet-doux (love letter). rare (Shakespeare). A kind of fish, esp. a red herring. Make a capon of; to castrate.

A revolving barrel on a vertical axis for winding cable etc., esp. on board ship; worked by persons walking round pushing bars fitting into the barrel, or by electricity, steam etc. A revolving spindle on a tape recorder etc.
Fond of taking exception or raising objections; carping. Apt or intended to deceive; fallacious, misleading. Capacious (rare - only in Shakespeare)
An Eastern inn with a large inner court where caravans rest.
A small light fast ship, chiefly Spanish or Portuguese, of the 15th to the 17th centuries.
A disinfectant soap or acid containing phenol. Used to make Chloraseptic, aspirin, weedkiller and Bakelite, the world's first completely synthetic plastics (when combined with formaldehyde).
A red precious stone, spec. one cut in a boss shape, esp. a garnet. A severe abscess, esp. on the neck; a multiple boil; a red facial spot or pimple.

A set of bells sounded either from a keyboard or mechanically. A tune played on such bells. A musical instrument or part of an organ designed to imitate a peal of bells. carillonneur - a person who plays such bells.
Decayed, rotten; affected with caries (decay of a tooth or bone).
A crimson pigment obtained from cochineal; carminic acid. The color of this. Deep crimson.
A large merchant-ship equipped for warfare, esp. a Portuguese Indiaman; a galleon.
A measure of land equivalent to the area that could be plowed in a year by one plough and eight oxen, a plough-land. carucage - a feudal tax levied on each carucate of land.
A piece of armour to cover the head; a helmet. A helmet-like structure in zoology.
A decorated structure fashioned so as to carry the coffin or effigy of a distinguished person during a funeral service or a lying in state.
A condition of trance or seizure with loss of sensation or consciousness and abnormal maintenance of posture. Comprehension, apprehension. cataleptic (adj. and n.).
A boy kept for homosexual practices; the passive partner in anal intercourse.
The third part of the ancient drama, in which the action is heightened for the catastrophe.
A hat, a cap (Irish).
Raise an unnecessary or frivolous objection (at, about). (verb) Such an objection. (noun)
Full of cavils (frivolous objections), apt to cavil. (-ing, -ation, -ous)
Swiftness, speed. A particular speed.
Fault-finding, severely critical; inclined to disapproval. Befitting a censor, grave, severe. rare.
(Of) the color of a cloudless sky; deep blue, azure. Also caerulean.
A part of a church near the altar, reserved for the clergy, choir, etc., and usually enclosed.
A personal name for a domestic rooster.
(Hindi) A narcotic resin from the flower-heads of hemp; cannabis resin. (also churrus).
Orig., a cemetery. Now (more fully charnel-house) a house or vault in which dead bodies or bones are piled. Sepulchral, deathlike, ghastly. A hinge, esp. that of a helmet.
Sorrowful, anxious; grievous. Dear, cherished. Cautious, wary, shy, fastidious; frugal, sparing, ungenerous (followed by about, in, of (doing))
Adhering to chiliasm, the doctrine of the millenium, the belief that Christ will reign in bodily presence on earth for a thousand years.
Divination by inspection of the hand, palmistry. (-er)(-tic(-al))(-tist)
A hunting cry. A chase, pursuit, hunt. The face (slang). Chase, harry, worry, trouble, harass. Race, scamper. (chiv - alt of shiv)
A kind of shoe raised above the ground by a cork sole or the like.
A pupa, esp. of a butterfly or moth, the hard sheath of this. Also fig., a quiescent transitional form.
The scar of a healed wound, burn, etc.; a scar on the bark of a tree. A mark or impression resembling a scar.
(Italian, pron. tee-tse-ro-ne) A guide who understands and explains antiquities etc. To act as a cicerone to. Ciceronian - pertaining to or in the style of Cicero, eloquent, classical, rhythmical.
Scimitar; a saber with a much-curved blade having the blade on the convex side, esp. used among Persians and Arabs.
Native mercury sulfide, a bright red mineral, used as a pigment, vermilion. (noun or adjective)

Any of several carnivorous mammals of Asia and Africa, which include genets and mongooses. A strong musky perfume obtained from the anal glands of these animals. (also verb - perfume with civet) (French) A highly seasoned stew of hare, venison, etc.
A soft white or pale blue-grey color, a Chinese porcelain glaze of this color.
(also clubber) Mud, soft dirt, wet clay. Curdle, turn sour.

The upper part of the nave, choir, and transepts of any large church, containing a series of windows, clear of the roofs of the aisles, admitting light to the central parts of the building. A similar feature in other buildings. A raised section of a railway-carriage roof containing small windows or ventilators.
An underground conduit for drainage, a sewer. A common cavity for the release of digestive and urogenital products in birds, reptiles, amphibians, most fish and monotremes.
In French, a beggar or vagrant. (fem. clocharde)
A bell-glass, a small translucent (esp. glass) cover for forcing or protecting outdoor plants. (Cloche hat) A woman's close-fitting bell-shaped hat.
A medicine injected into the rectum, an enema, occas. a suppository. To treat with a clyster.
A ship's small boat, esp. one towed behind a vessel going up or down river.
(Also cenobite) A member of a monastic community, a hermit (eremite).

(Also coigne or quoin) A projecting corner, a cornerstone, an angle. A wedge. coign of vantage (Shakes.) - a place affording a good view of something. To secure or raise with a quoin or wedge. (also foll. by 'up').
(also custrel) An attendant on a knight or man-at-arms. As a term of reproach: knave, fool. Now rare.
Discourses, dialogues (spoken or written), acts of conversing; conversations. Colloquial - belonging to familiar speech and writing, not used in formal or elevated language.
Florid passages in vocal music, with runs, trills, etc.; the singing of these. A singer of coloratura, esp. a soprano.
Courtesy, civility, kindly and considerate behavior towards others. comity of nations - friendly recognition as far as is practicable by nations of each other's laws and usages.
Threatening of divine vengeance, esp. a recital of divine threats against sinners in the Anglican liturgy for Ash Wednesday.
Beneficial, profitable, useful, convenient, serviceable, spec. convenient as accommodation or shelter, roomy, spacious.
An elderly man who lavishes gifts on a younger woman. A person in a cabaret act, radio or television show, etc. who introduces the performers, comments on the turns, etc.
(Of a quality, circumstance, etc.) occurring along with something else, accompanying. noun - an attendant quality, state, circumstance, etc.; an accompaniment. (-ly)

Of punishment, retribution, etc.: appropriate to the crime, well-deserved and severe. condignity - Grace earned by works, as opposed to that freely given; merit acquired by man through actions performed in reliance on the Holy Spirit.

(Also conge) Permission (for any act). (rare) Ceremonious leave-taking. Formal permission to depart. A bow. (rare). In modern French, unceremonious dismissal. Water in which rice has been boiled (congee).
An association of booksellers who sold or printed books for their common advantage. A European sea-eel caught for food.
A collection of disparate or unsorted items; a rag-bag. (also congery)
Related by descent from a common ancestor, of or pertaining to blood relationship.

Obstinate disobedience to authority. Contumacious - Scornfully insulting, insolent, reproachful. Contumely - (An instance of) contemptuously insulting language or treatment, scornful and humiliating rudeness. (noun)
A physical or mental disturbance.
An aggregation of contiguous towns or urban areas forming a single community in some respects.
An adversary. A partner, a colleague; a companion; spec. a lover, a spouse. A man. (colloquial or contemptuous)

(of an animal) living in or feeding on dung. capromania - an obsession with faeces. (copromanie) (Greek kopros - dung). coprophagist - involving or engaging in the eating of dung. (coprophagous, coprophagy) coprophilia - undue interest in faeces and defecation.

A horizontal, usually molded projection crowning the outside of a building or structure; the uppermost part of an entablature, above the frieze. An ornamental molding running around the wall of a room near the ceiling, a picture rail. An overhanging ledge of ice or snow at a cliff edge.
A road along the edge of a cliff, any coastal road with panoramic views. (also corniche road).
A day's unpaid work required of a vassal by a feudal lord; forced labour exacted by or as in its place. That on public roads in France before 1776; fig. an unpleasant duty; an onerous task.
Esp. of an animal: lying down; couching. In heraldry, of an animal: lying on its belly with its head up. Lying hidden, lurking.
Cheat, trick, (of, out of), beguile ('into'). Deceive, mislead. cozenage (n), cozener (n).
Break wind. Of a bombardier beetle: eject a pungent fluid with a sudden sharp report. Make a crackling sound; (of the lungs) make the sound of crepitation. crepitant (adj.).
A piece of enclosed land used for tillage or pasture, esp. a plot of arable land attached to a house. A smallholding worked by a tenant, esp. in Scotland. A crypt; a cavern.
Testicles, balls (antiquated).
Inordinate desire to appropriate another's wealth or possessions; greed for gain.
Native cuprous oxide, a red cubic mineral important as an ore of copper. cupric - of copper in the divalent state. cuprous - of the nature of copper.
The office or position of curate (a person holding a spiritual charge, pastor, clergyman).
A spittoon.
A young swan.
The constellation Ursa Minor, or the polestar which it contains. (rare) A thing which serves for guidance or direction. A thing or person at the center of admiration or attraction.
A member of an Indian or Burmese band of armed robbers. To plunder as a dacoit.

A metrical foot consisting of one long syllable followed by two short syllables, or of one stressed syllable followed by two unstressed syllables; a verse composed of or containing such feet. A date (fruit). A terminal part of a jointed claw, limb, etc.
Coat or cover with plaster, mortar, clay, etc. Material for daubing. Cover or paint crudely or inartistically.
The title of the eldest son of the King of France (1349-1830), crown prince.
In Judaism, to recite the prescribed liturgical prayers.

A (curved) crane mounted on a ship for hoisting objects inboard or outboard; orig. one mounted at the bow for use in hoisting the anchor. Now freq. either of a pair of cranes used for suspending or lowering a ship's boat.

(Orig. military, of troops etc.) emerge from a narrow or confined space into open ground, issue (of from a mouth or outlet (also foll. by 'on')). Lead into open ground, provide an outlet for, pour forth. debouchment (n).

deckle - a device which confines the pulp and so limits the size of a piece of paper, consisting of either a frame or mould used in hand paper-making, or in full deckle strap or machine manufacture, a continuous belt on either side of the machine's wire. deckled - formed by a deckle. deckle-edged - the rough uncut edge of handmade paper.
Downward slope, inclination, sloping ground. declivous, declivitous (-ly)
To subtract part of an account from the whole; to reduce or curtail. Misappropriate property in one's charge.
The action of throwing a thing or (usu. fig.) a person out of a window.
Move, step, esp. a diplomatic action.
The class of women of doubtful reputation and social standing; the class of kept women or loosely of prostitutes. Any social group regarded as behaving with doubtful propriety or legality.
Dernier - last, ultimate, final. dernier cri - the latest fashion. dernier mot - the last word. dernier resort - final refuge; last court of appeal.

Repeal or abrogate in part (a law etc.), destroy or impair the force, effect, or authority of. Detract from, disparage, depreciate. Take away (something from a thing) so as to lessen or impair it. Degenerate, deviate (from) correct behavior. Lessened in authority. Debased.

A melodious accompaniment to a simple theme sung or played above it. The soprano or highest part of the score in part-singing. Musical composition, harmony. An instrumental prelude consisting of variations on a given theme. A discourse in a theme or subject, an observation, a criticism, a remark. A variation from typical or customary.
The chaste and virtuous wife of Shakespeare's Othello, the Moorish general.
Remove the moisture from, dry up, esp. for foodstuffs for preservation. Deprive of energy or feeling, make impersonal. A desiccated substance or product.
The action of discontinuing something; discontinuance (of), protracted cessation ('from'). A state of disuse. The action of passing into disuse.

Skipping about or jumping from one thing to another; pursuing an irregular or erratic course; going constantly from one subject to another; digressive. Lacking a fixed plan or purpose; unmethodical; occurring irregularly, intermittent. Occurring randomly in isolation, occasional; disconnected.
Thrust or push down; formerly, also subdue, defeat. Thrust out or away; expel.
Any of a class of deities in Vedic mythology; any of the lower-level gods in Hinduism and Buddhism.
Move or slope downwards. Cease, leave off. A slope. A stop or cessation.
(adj.) Of or on the right-hand side of a person or thing, esp. of a shield, etc. (opp. sinister) Of an omen: seen or heard on the right-hand side, hence auspicious.

Something worn on the head as a symbol of honor, esp. royalty, a crown (chiefly poetic). A wreath of leaves or flowers worn around the head. Royal or imperial sovereignty; something conferring dignity, a crowning glory, an adornment on the top of something.
Of, pertaining to, or of the nature of logical disputation. Fond of or practising logical disputation.

The interval of an octave; the consonance of two notes an octave apart; complete musical harmony (rare). The combination of notes or parts in a harmonious whole; a melody; a swelling sound, a grand burst of harmony; a rich, deep burst of sound, the whole range of notes in the scale.
Having the character or manner of a teacher, intended to instruct; having instruction as an ulterior purpose. A didactic or treatise. didactics: the art of teaching.
Lacking confidence or trust (in); distrustful, mistrustful (of). Lacking self-confidence; timid in one's dealings with others.
Tending to cause delay, having the purpose of gaining time. Given to or characterized by delay; slow, tardy.
Put out of countenance, abash, embarrass. Discourage with cold looks, express disfavour of, refuse to sanction or allow. The fact or an act of discountenancing; disfavour or disapprobation shown.

Ill humor, bad temper, disturbance of the bodily humors. Disturbed condition of the body or mind; ill health, intoxication. To disturb the temper or feelings of. A disproportionate mixing of parts. A method of painting in which powder colors are mixed with a glutinous substance dissolved in water.

Chiefly astronomy. Performed in or occupying one day. Belonging to each day, occurring or (arch.) published every day, daily; varying with a one-day period. Of the day rather than the night; of an animal etc., active during the day. A book containing the daytime canonical hours. A daybook, a diary. A newspaper or publication esp. one published daily (rare).

A megalithic structure found esp. in Britain and France, consisting of a large flat stone supported on stone slabs set vertically in the ground forming a burial chamber, probably orig. covered by an earth mound.
Sulky, pettish, haughty, saucy. Fastidious. Sluggish. Delicate, feeble; difficult to rear. Dry, not raining.
Any of several marine fishes characterized by thin, deep bodies. (John Dory) - e.g. A skiff, esp. a flat-bottomed one.
Pleasant, sweet. Quiet, sober, sedate. doucely (adv.), douceness (n.).

Refuse, rubbish, worthless matter, esp. as contrasted with or separated from something of value. Foreign matter mixed with anything; dregs of wine, chaff of corn, etc. Impurities separated from metal by melting.
A nymph supposed to inhabit trees; a wood nymph.
An older woman acting as governess and companion to one or more girls, esp. in a Spanish family. A chaperon.
Authentic / authentically; genuine (ly); typical (ly). (adj. + adv.)
Radiance, dazzling effect, brilliant display. Social distinction, celebrity, renown. Conspicuous success, universal acclamation (with éclat).

Of or belonging to the whole Christian world or the universal Church. In recent use, freq. marked by ecumenism, seeking (worldwide) Christian unity transcending doctrinal differences, of or representing Christians of several denominations, interdenominational. Universal, general, worldwide.
Lead or draw out, in medicine, to remove by drawing out. Bring out or develop from latent or rudimentary existence, elicit, evoke. Infer (a principle etc.) 'from' a set of data. educible (adj.)

Bloom, burst out into, or, as into flower. Turn to fine powder through loss of water or exposure to air (crystalline substances); (of salt): be carried in solution to the surface of the ground. Blossom out; become manifest.
Weird, ghostly, unnatural, hideous.
Of the philosophical Greek school of Elea, dated 6th and 5th centuries BC.

Pass over in silence, suppress, strike out, or omit, often by joining several items together. Omit (a sound, syllable, etc.) by elision. Annul, quash, do away with. Make of no account, weaken or destroy (the force of evidence).

An omission of a sound, syllable, etc., running together the sounds on either side of it; an omission of a passage in a book etc. Elysian - Of, pertaining to, or resembling Elysium, the paradisal home of the blessed after death in Greek mythology; also a state of perfect happiness.
Something inserted or moving in another, esp. the piston of a syringe. The blood clot or other object or substance which causes embolism.

An opening in a parapet that widens toward the outside, made to fire a gun through. A slanting or bevelling of the wall on each side of a door or window opening so as to form a recess; the area contained between such walls. The angle between adjacent teeth. To provide with an embrasure.

Alter (a text) to remove errors and corruptions; gen. to free from faults, correct, rectify. emendate - emend. emendative (adj.). emendation - reformation, improvement of corruptions of a text by alteration and correction.
A substance that causes vomiting when ingested, esp. one given for this purpose. Causing vomiting; fig. sickening, revoltingly sentimental.
A person who exercises power or influence though holding no official position. A confidential advisor.
Principal, important, valuable. Exalted, important; distinguished in position, attainments, or character. Remarkable, noteworthy. High, lofty; towering above the surroundings.
Profit or gain arising from office or employment, reward, remuneration. Benefit, comfort.
A formal or high-flown expression of praise, a panegyric.
The custom of marrying only within the limits of a local community, clan, or tribe. The fusion of reproductive cells from related individuals.

adj.: lacking moral, literary, or artistic vigor, spiritless, effeminate, lacking physical strength. vr. to: deprive of vigor, use vitality, debilitate, weaken mentally, morally, or (formerly) physically. Destroy the force or authority of an argument, doctrine, etc. Cut the tendons of a horse.
Mental weariness and dissatisfaction arising from lack of occupation or interest; boredom. (also ennuyé) ennuied (v. trans). ennuyant - that gives rise to ennui; boring.

In Aristotle's use: the condition in which a potentiality has become an actuality; spec. the essential nature or informing principle of a living thing; the soul. A supposed vital principle that guides the development and functioning of an organism. In Leibniz's use: a monad (absolute indivisible entity (n)).
A storehouse for the temporary deposit of goods. A commercial center to which goods are brought for import and export.

The numeric extent to which a system's thermal energy is unavailable for conversion into mechanical work; how much heat cannot be turned into energy; equivalently, the degree of disorder of a system. A logarithmic measure of the average information rate of a message or language.
Shocking (to conventional persons), daring.
A young man; spec. in ancient Greece, one from 18 to 20 years old undergoing military training.
A fold of skin from the upper eyelid that covers the inner angle of the eye, occurring in Mongolians and as a congenital anomaly in other people. epicanthic
A member of a succeeding and less distinguished generation.
A short poem leading up to and ending in a witty or ingenious turn of thought. A concise pointed saying.
An inscription, esp. one on a tombstone, building, statue, etc.; a legend on a coin.
The branch of philosophy that deals with the varieties, grounds, and validity of knowledge.
The second part of a play, in which the action begins; the part of a play etc. where the plot thickens.
Of motion, temperature, the feelings, etc.: uniform, free from fluctuation or variation, free from inequalities, equally proportioned.

Apparatus of war; all an army requires for encampment, transport, etc. Small articles of domestic furniture, as china, glassware, etc.; articles for personal ornament or use, or a case of these. The appurtenances of rank, social position, etc.; a carriage and horses with attendants.
Made or used as a (usu. inferior) substitute for something else. An ersatz thing (n).
Expel or emit violently. Of a person: belch. eructation - belching, a belch. Volcanic eruption. Material that is emitted.
A person who prefers present advantage to permanent rights or integrity; Isaac's elder twin son, who sold his birthright.

The branch of theology that deals with the last four things (death, judgment, heaven, and hell) and the final destiny of the soul and of humankind. A doctrine or belief about the second coming or the kingdom of God.
Fit for food, eatable. (adj.) Something fit for food, eatable. (noun) (esp. a vegetable).

The shield or shield-shaped surface on which a coat of arms is depicted, the shield together with its armorial bearings; a representation of this, a coat of arms, a shield-shaped charge. A shield-shaped area or object; a protective plate, spec. one around a keyhole. The middle of a ship's stern where the name is placed. fig. reputation.

A fruit tree or ornamental shrub trained on a lattice or a framework of stakes. A row of trees or shrubs trained in this way. A lattice or framework, or one of the stakes, on which a tree or shrub is trained. Train as an espalier.
Expectation, hope. obs. exc. historical as the motto of the Percy family, used as a battle-cry (Shakes. Henry IV).
(Also étagère) A piece of furniture with a number of open shelves on which to display ornaments etc.
Make (a plant) pale by excluding light, give a pale and sickly hue to (a person); cause to lose vigor or substance.
The quality, esp. of spoken words, of having a pleasant sound, the pleasing effect of sounds free from harshness. The tendency to phonetic change giving easier pronunciation.
A jug with a wide mouth, esp. a water jug of the kind formerly used in bedrooms.
'Go higher!' Curled shavings of soft wood for stuffing, packing, etc. A person or thing that reaches or aspires to reach higher. A 3-point size type (very small).
Remove portions of the skin from, esp. by corrosive action or abrasion. Peel off skin, flay. (fig.) Make a scathing attack on.
Utter curses, invoke evil upon; express loathing for, abhor.
An exposition, esp. of Scripture; a gloss; an explanatory note for discourse. (-te) - A person skilled in exegesis. (-tic) - Explanatory (of, to).
Funeral rites; a funeral ceremony. A funeral ode. Also exequies.
A stage direction (actors, or the characters whose names follow) leave the stage. exeunt omnes - all leave the stage.
Wander about at will, roam unrestrained (rare). Speak or write at great length on a topic, dilate (on). Extend or diffuse a thing so that it covers a wide area (rare).

Expiate - Put an end to pain, etc. by death, extinguish rage by suffering to the full; cleanse person or place of guilt or pollution, by ritual ceremonies; atone or make amends (for), extinguish the guilt arising from a sin; pay the penalty of an offense.

Unfold, unwrap, open out (a bud, leaf, etc.), spread out, display, make larger in area or volume. Explain, give details of, make clear one's meanings. Unravel, solve, disentangle, extricate from (a difficulty, etc.)

Ask for, demand, ask how or why. Discourse, talk earnestly in order to protest after person's action, or to dissuade him or her (with, about, on, etc.). Complain of a grievance; remonstrate about (with someone); debate as an aggrieved person.
Purge or cleanse (the body, etc.) of excremental material. Remove from (a book) passages regarded as objectionable. expurgator, expurgatory, expurgation.
Root out, eradicate, get rid of (a heresy, vice, or other immaterial thing). Make extinct (from, out of), kill all the members (of a race, group, etc.). Destroy totally.
Let or force out a fluid, esp. blood, from the vessel that naturally contains it. Of blood, lava, etc.: flow out; undergo extravasation, an escape or effusion of blood or other fluid.
Howl, cry out.
Overflowing; superabundant.
A district outside a city or town, esp. a prosperous one beyond the suburbs.
Burn up (rare).
Strip a person of, divest or deprive of.
Cast skins, shells, or other shed outer parts of animals, whether recent or fossil; sloughed skins.
The nest of a bird of prey, esp. an eagle, or of any other bird which builds high up; fig. a human residence built at a great height. A young bird of prey.
A person who relates or composes fables or legends. A person who invents dishonest stories; a liar.
Made by human skill or effort, not naturally occurring or produced. (rare) Made for a special purpose; not genuine, not natural or spontaneous; artificial.
Disposed, inclined, eager (to do). Happy, well-pleased (to do).
A broad curved sword with the edge on the convex side. Later, a sword of any kind. A billhook.
A temple. (Latin) A flag, banner, pennant. A weathercock. (Norse)
Sullen, shy. farouchely (adv.)
A confused group; a medley, a mixture, a hotchpotch.
A smith who shoes horses; a person who treats the injuries and diseases of horses. An official with care of the horses in a cavalry regiment. Farriery - veterinary surgery with regard to horses.
A long faggot (bundle) used for engineering purposes and (esp. in war) for lining trenches, filling ditches, etc. Fill up, protect or strengthen with fascines.
The apex, the summit. The ridge or gable end of a roof, a pediment. Fastigiate - sloping upwards or tapering to a point (rare); having a flat surface at the top (rare).
A kind of mirage most frequently seen in the Strait of Messina between Italy and Sicily, attributed in early times to fairy agency; an illusion.
Having chinks or clefts; cracked.
Of or pertaining to the west wind, gentle, propitious.
Of or pertaining to fever; produced by or indicative of fever, feverish. (febrility)
Feeble, futile, ineffective, aimless; irresponsible.
Containing or of the nature of feces or dregs; filthy, turbid, foul, fetid.

Happy; showing or marked by great happiness; also fortunate, prosperous, successful. Of an action, manner, etc.: very apt, well suited to the occasion. Of a person: happy or pleasantly apt in expression, manner, or style; pleasing, delightful.
Womankind. Earlier, spec. the Amazons, also, their land. feminiety: womanliness, womanishness. feminal: of or pertaining to women, womanly, feminine.
A metal ring or cap for strengthening, esp. one for preventing the end of a stick, tube, etc from splitting or wearing. Provide or fit with a ferrule.

Fenestrate - Having an opening, provide with small holes or openings; perforate. Fenestration - The arrangement of windows in a building, the operation of cutting an artificial opening into the ear. Defenestration - Throwing a thing or (usu.) person out of a window (defenestrate).
(Also foetor) A foul or offensive smell; a stench.
Fated to die, at the point of death, as manifested by strange exultant behavior supposedly portending death. Disordered in mind, behaving strangely, like a person about to die.
(Also fillibeg, philabeg) The gathered and belted lower part of a plaid; a kilt.
Ornamental work, orig. with beads or precious stones, of fine (usu. gold or silver) wire, twisted, plaited, and soldered into a delicate openwork design; anything delicate resembling this.

A smart blow (with the fist etc.). (rare) Bending the last joint of the finger against the thumb and suddenly releasing it, a smart stroke or tap given this way. A trifle; a moment. A stimulus; an incentive. to fillip.
A fiery dragon in German mythology. A fiery meteor. A person with a fiery red nose. rare (Shakes.).
Religious term for the sky or the heavens. Ancient: the boundary between the ocean and the sky.

Orig., a part that widens out (now only in a vein of ore). A projecting flat rim, collar, or rib, serving esp. for strengthening, attachment, or (on a wheel) maintaining position on a rail. Also, a rim or fan standing out from the main part of a natural object. Alter a sound recording by copying sound of a particular but varying frequency.
Yellowish, tawny.
A lancet used for bloodletting.
A flower-shaped ornament, used esp. in architecture or printing, as a device on coins, etc. A small pastry puff used for garnishing.
An abstract method of working with analytical data.
Full of bends and curves; winding, sinuous. Moving in bends or waves; undulating (rare).
Flattery, empty compliment, nonsense; trifles, useless trappings or ornaments. A dish made with boiled jelly, oat, or wheatmeal; sweet dishes made with milk, flour, eggs, gelatin, etc.

(Arch. from Fugger, Augsburg merchants) - A person given to underhand practices for the sake of gain; esp. a low-class lawyer, etc. A petty chapman, a pedlar. A middleman between a nail-maker and a wholesale nail merchant.
A former size of paper for printing, 13½ x 17 inches; also, a former size of writing paper, 13 x 8 inches. A fool's or jester's cap, usually hung with bells; also, a dunce's cap.
A stream or rush of fresh water flowing into the sea; a small freshwater stream. A flood of a river caused by heavy rain or melted snow.
An emotional thrill; a shiver of excitement.
(Excessively) complimentary, (too) effusive, lavish, or flattering, overdone. Full and plump; overgrown, overfed.
Reddish-yellow, dull yellowish brown; tawny.
Of, pertaining to, or appropriate to a funeral; gloomy, dark, dismal, mournful. (-ly)
A gathered or pleated strip or border on a skirt or petticoat, a flounce, a ruffle; (in pl. derog) showy ornamentation or trimming on a garment. A seaweed with large frilly fronds.
The elongated body section of an airplane, containing the crew and passengers or cargo.
Cudgel; beat. (fustigation)
adj.- Valiant; sturdy. Lively, brisk, full of high spirits; bright or colorful in appearance. noun - Orig., a valiant man. Now only, a lively man of fashion and pleasure.

A brace or pair of braces to support the trousers. Also variant of gallows - Fit only to be hanged, wicked, atrocious. Now milder; high-spirited, dashing, full of mischief, cheeky, impish. Extremely great, fine, or handsome.
Play games, comp; frolic (chiefly as gameling).
Street urchin, waif. A streetwise or impudent child. (noun + adj.) gamine - a female gamin. A small, attractively informal, mischievous, or elfish young woman.

A turret projecting from the top of a tower or from the parapet of a fortification, a watchtower. A wretched room or apartment on the top floor of a house, esp. one partly or wholly within the roof; an attic.
Extremely cold, cold as ice.
Any plant with four- or five-lobed corollas freq. of a brilliant deep blue, chiefly growing in damp, alpine places. A bitter tonic or liqueur made from gentian root.
(also giglet). Originally, a lewd wanton woman; a giddy, laughing, romping girl. (rare) Applied to a man: excessively given to merriment. giglot-wench, giglet-flirt, giglot-fair.
(Also gillie) A Scottish Highland chief's attendant. A man or boy attending a hunter or fisherman. A gill of liquor.
A kind of small boring-tool, usu. with a cross-piece handle and a screw at the pointed end. Of an eye, etc.: piercing, penetrating; squinting. Turn an anchor round by rotating the stock.
(Anglo-Irish) a young girl.
Of a dull greyish-green or greyish-blue; esp. in botany, covered with a powdery bloom as of grapes.

A short pithy statement expressing a general truth; a maxim, an aphorism. A member of a legendary subterranean race of diminutive beings who guard the earth's treasure. Zurich gnome or gnomes of Zurich - colloq. term for international, esp. Swiss financiers or bankers, regarded as sinister.

A pillar, rod, etc., which shows the time of day by casting its shadow on a marked surface, esp. the pin or triangular plate of a sundial. The nose. The part of a parallelogram left after a similar parallelogram is taken away from one corner. An L-shaped bar, as a carpenter's square. A guide, an indicator or indicating instrument. A rule, a canon of belief or action.
In a godly fashion.
Luscious, delightful.
Any of various blowing, spouting, blunt-nosed cetaceans of the family Delphinidae, esp. Risso's dolphin or killer whales. A person given to puffing and blowing.
A manual of black magic supposedly used to cast spells, invoke demons, etc.

A denomination of coin issued from the 13th cent. in any of various European countries, having from the 14th cent. a theoretical value equal to that of 1/3 oz of silver but varying in actual intrinsic value. An English silver coin, issued 1351-1662, in value equal to four pennies. A drachma, a small sum or amount.
Karl Marx's outline of the critique of political economy.
A small silverside fish of Californian coasts, Leuresthes tenuis, which comes ashore to spawn.
In France, (a) marionette show or drama resembling Punch & Judy. Also Grand Guignol.
A circular movement or turn, a revolution, a gyration. A circle, a spiral, a vortex. A circular pattern of surface currents around an ocean basin. To turn or whirl around, gyrate.
(Arabic) The body of traditions concerning the sayings and doings of the Prophet Muhammad, now considered to be second in authority to the Koran and to embody the sunna.

Any of various blue-grey and silver gadoid fishes of shallow temperate seas, most conventionally fished. Either of two reddish-brown gadoid food fishes of the NW Atlantic. A short firearm used in the 16th century.
A filament or fiber, a barb or fiber of a feather. To drag, usu. with friction or scraping of the ground.

A stock character of the witty servant in Italian comedy and later French light comedy; also a mute character in English pantomime, and a mischievous buffoon, usu. wearing a mask and particolored tights. Gaily colored; having distinctively variegated markings.
A parching dusty land-wind on the W. African coast from December to February. (harmattan wind)
A haggard or ill-tempered old woman.
Rough and hard to the touch or taste, esp. from lack of moisture. Dry, rough, coarse. (hasky)
A firm tuft or clump of grass, etc., esp. as occurring in boggy ground. A thick firm cushion, formerly stuffed with straw, used to rest the feet on or, esp. in church, to kneel on. (hassocky)
(also hawse) The neck. A narrow neck of land or channel of water; a col or narrow ridge joining two summits. The throat, the gullet. To embrace, to clasp.
A large rope or small cable used for mooring or anchoring.
A conical heap of hay in a field. hayrick - a haystack. haybag - (derog. slang) a woman.
A stratum of the ionosphere between the lowest (D) and highest (F) layers, able to reflect long radio waves. Also called E-layer, Kennelly layer.
A great public sacrifice, strictly of a hundred oxen, among the ancient Greeks and Romans; gen. a religious sacrifice; a large number of animals set apart for sacrifice. A sacrifice of many victims.
The emigration of Muhammad from Mecca to Medina in 622; the Muslim era reckoned from this. Any exodus or departure.

Plants whose flowers turn towards the sun; their scent; their bluish purple color. A green variety of chalcedony quartz; bloodstone. An ancient sundial, showing when the sun reached solstice. A telescope and movable mirror reflecting the sun's rays as a signal or for surveying.

A spiral ornament, a volute, specifically, each of the eight smaller volutes under the abacus of a Corinthian capital. An object of coiled form, either round an axis (as a corkscrew) or in one plane (as a watchspring); a 3-D curve on a conical or cylindrical surface which becomes a straight line when the surface is unwound into a plane.
Orig. the root of one of two poisonous and purgative plants reputed in classical times to cure insanity. Now, any of various plants of the buttercup family.
Semicircular. Hemidemisemiquaver—a quaver with four hooks (musical note), i.e. the smallest sound imaginable.
Of or pertaining to (theories of) interpretation, esp. of Scripture.
Strive, exert oneself, pant. Hasten, hurry, go quickly (to). Advance, quickly, make progress, prosper. Cause to hasten, urge on, bring quickly (away). Make quickly (one's way).

Pertaining to or used by a priestly class, used in connection with sacred subjects; spec. designating a style of ancient Egyptian writing consisting of abridged forms of hieroglyphics. Characteristic of a sacred person or duty. Priestly, sacerdotal. Of a style of art adhering to early methods as laid down by religious tradition.
An official expounder of sacred mysteries or ceremonies, esp. in ancient Greece; an initiating or presiding priest. An expounder of sacred mysteries, an interpreter of an esoteric principle.
(Of hair) grey or white with age; grey-haired, ancient, venerable. Also old and trite. Grey, greyish-white, esp. with frost. Mouldy, musty, nasty.
A rustic, clown.
An American Indian (esp. Navajo) hut made from logs, earth, etc.
Ordering or encouraging a camel to move, esp. to get down on its knees for mounting or dismounting. To direct with the word hooshtah.
Characteristic of homily, religious discourse. The art of preaching.
Exhortatory. hortative: exhortative adj (esp. of a speech).
Any of the virgins of the Muslim paradise, promised as wives to believers; a voluptuously beautiful woman.

Belief in the humanity but not divinity of Christ. The quality of devotion to human interests and welfare. Devotion to studies promoting culture, esp. Renaissance. Concerned with human rather than divine matters, rational ways of solving problems; humankind as responsible and progressive intellectual beings.
The organic constituent of soil, formed by the decomposition of plant materials.
A lesser form of the given name used in more intimate situations as a form of endearment; a pet name; diminutive.

Blood, a liquid likened to the blood of animals. A watery discharge from a wound or sore. A fluid supposed to flow like blood in the veins of the gods. An emanation from magma supposed by some to cause granitization.
A screen separating the sanctuary or altar from the nave in some Orthodox churches and bearing icons.
Indwelling, inherent (in), (of God) permanently pervading and sustaining the universe. Of an action that is performed entirely within the mind of the subject, and produces no external effect.
Surround with a wall or walls, enclose within walls; confine, build into or entomb in a wall.
Ask or request of a person persistently or pressingly. Urge or impel a person or thing. Solicit for purposes of prostitution. Ask or beg for a thing persistently, burden, trouble, pester.
(An act of) wilful and fraudulent deception. imposturous (adj.).
Flesh-colored, crimson. Orig., in allusion to Shakes (sense B). Dye flesh-colored or crimson, as in MacBeth, stain with blood. Flesh-color, crimson, blood red (n.).

Just begun, incipient, rudimentary, not yet fully formed or developed. Chaotic, confused; (of thought or language) incoherent. To produce the first stages of, commence, cause to begin, bring about, make a beginning; commence.
Crude, unpolished, unrefined, (esp. of literary or artistic works) badly constructed or composed. inconditely (adv.).

Of, pertaining to, or constituting a transitional or initial stage of a process. Also, marginal, incidental, insignificant. Of, pertaining to, or situated at a limen, occupying a position on or on both sides of, a boundary or threshold.
Paint a picture or portrait. Depict, make visible, portray (esp. a person) in words. (Rare) To illuminate a manuscript, adorn with gold or bright color.
A book printed at an early date, esp. before 1501. pl. incunabula: the early stages of development of a thing.

(Also, earlier, endite) Put into words, compose (a poem, story, speech, etc.); give a literary form to; express or describe in a literary composition. Put into writing; write (a letter, etc.). Speak, suggest, or inspire (a form of words to be repeated or written down); dictate. Enjoin as a law or precept; dictate to a person.

Too great to be expressed in words; unutterable, indefinable, indescribable. Not to be uttered; not to be disclosed. Unpronounceable. Beyond description. effable- that can or may be expressed or described in words.
Unable to be resisted or avoided; inescapable, indelible. (-ly, -ility)
Unable to be cleared of clouds or mist. Inexplicable.
To be inherent in; to exist as an essential, permanent, or characteristic attribute, quality, etc.
Unfriendly, hostile (to). Adverse, injurious, harmful (to). (also inimicitious, inimicous) inimicality, inimically, inimicalness.
Surpassing or defying imitation; without compare, peerless. (adj. + noun) Inimical- unfriendly, hostile, adverse, injurious (to).
Distinguished, eminent, remarkable. A badge, ensign, or emblem.
Of a difficulty, problem, etc.: unable to be surmounted or overcome. Rare: Unconquerable, invincible; unable to be vanquished; unable to be surpassed.

Something with which an object is covered, enclosed, or clothed; a covering, a coating. A natural outside covering of part of an animal or plant body, as a skin, husk, rind, etc. (also tegument, now also.)

An interval during which the normal government is suspended, esp. during the period between the end of a monarch's rule and the accession of his or her successor. any period of cessation or suspension of rule, authority, etc.
Not disposed of by will; belonging to the estate of an intestate. (a) Not having made a will. (n)
Beguile, deceive. Win over or capture by deceitful allurement; entice, seduce. Entrap, ensnare, entangle. Guilefully draw (a person) (into, from, to, etc.) an action, conduct, place, etc.
Long-standing, chronic, deep-rooted, ingrained; bad habit, prejudice, etc. Habitual, hardened, obstinate.
(also irenical)- peaceful, conciliatory; tending to promote peace, esp. in theological or ecclesiastical disputes.

Iris- A variety of quartz (formerly, any mineral) producing iridescent reflections. Any plant of the large genus Iris. A rainbow, esp. personified (freq. Iris). A flat circular colored membrane suspended vertically in the aqueous humour of the eye.

A firm whitish semitransparent substance, a comparatively pure form of gelatin, obtained from the swim-bladders of some freshwater fishes, esp. sturgeon, used in cookery. Also, similar substances made from hides, hoofs, etc. Mica (from its similarity in appearance).

In chemistry, of two or more (series of) compounds: having comparable or related molecular structures, now usu. spec. (of compounds) having identical molecular structure but different atoms of the same valency at some position(s) in the molecule. Genetically identical, esp. as regards immunological factors, involving such individuals.
A piece of leg armour; a leg. (plural: -x)

An adherent of the Roman Catholic school of thought holding the doctrines of Cornelis Jansen, who maintained (claiming the support of St. Augustine) the necessariness and inability for good of the natural human will.
Having a dual function, purpose, attitude, etc. Also Janus-faced. (Of a material) having a double facing. (of a device) having a two-way action.

Without food, fasting, undernourished, hungry. Intellectually unsatisfying, lacking substance, shallow, simplistic, dull, dry, uninspired, vapid, puerile, childish, naive. Not nourishing or insubstantial; scanty; meagre, frugal; (of land) poor, barren.
A small Spanish horse, esp. a pacer.
A large wine bottle, equivalent to four ordinary bottles.
Of a person, their disposition: fond of joking; playful, waggish, jocular. Of speech, writing or action: of the nature of or containing a joke; said or done jokingly; playful, jocular. (-ly, -ness)
Feeling or expressing cheerfulness; mirthful, merry, light-hearted, pleasant, cheering, delightful. (-ly) (-ity)
Each of a series of parallel supporting beams of timber, steel, etc., to which floorboards, ceiling lathes, etc., are attached. To provide with or fix on joists.
A kind of narcissus with rushlike leaves and fragrant yellow flowers, used in perfumery. A pale yellow color. Of pale yellow (adj.).
The spiritual leader of a Khazar khaganate or kingdom, 7th–10th century Khazaria in the northern Caucasus.
(Also caracul) A breed of sheep with a coarse wiry fleece. Cloth or fur resembling the glossy curled fleece of a young lamb of this breed. karakul (adj.).
A small anchor with an iron stock for warping or hauling off after grounding. To warp or tow (a ship) by hauling in a hawser attached to a small anchor dropped at some distance.

The lengthwise timber or metal structure along the base of a ship or boat. A ship or vessel. A central ridge along the back of an animal or plant. A flat-bottomed boat, esp. of a kind used on the rivers Tyne and Wear in NE England for carrying coal and loading colliers. A red ocherous iron ore, used for marking, ruddle. Cool a hot liquid by stirring, skimming, etc., in order to prevent it from boiling over. Turn up the keel of, capsize, overturn. Use with over.

One or more light-armed Irish foot soldiers. The kernel of a nut. A grain (of wheat, sand, etc.). Cause to granulate, make (salt) into grains. (intr.) Of salt etc: to crystallize, become granular. Sprinkle or preserve with salt. Typography- part of a metal type projecting beyond the body or shank, as parts of some italic letters; cast with a kern or kerns. Meteorology- a suspended particle which acts as a nucleus for condensation.
A two-masted, fore-and-aft rigged sailing vessel (formerly used esp. for coastal trading) in which the mizzen-mast is shorter than the mainmast and stepped forward of the rudder post.
A chapped or ulcerated chilblain or blister, esp. one on the heel. A sore on the foot of a horse, sheep, etc. on the kibes of - on the heels of.
A chapped or ulcerated chilblain or blister, esp. one on the heel. A sore on the foot of a horse, sheep, etc. on the kibes of - on the heels of.
In Imperial Russia, a whip used to inflict punishment, often causing death. To flog someone with such a whip.
A powder, usually consisting of antimony sulfide or lead sulfide, used as eye makeup and as eye ointment, esp. in Eastern countries.
In German-speaking lands, a health resort, a spa, a watering-place.
Resembling tears, liable to exude in drops. Tearful, inclined to weep; of the eyes: full of tears. Calculated to provoke tears; sad, mournful. Lachrymary: a weeping ulcer. (-ly, -ity)
Of or pertaining to Laconia or its inhabitants; Spartan. Using few words; concise, terse, as Spartans.
A hiatus, a blank, a missing portion, esp. in a manuscript or text. (lacunae- plural). A gap, depression, space, or cavity in an organism, esp. in bone.
(Louisiana French) Something given as a bonus or gratuity; extra reward.
A plaything, a toy. Formerly also, a baby. (Norse)
Of a flame or light: playing lightly upon a surface without burning it; shining with a soft clear light and without fierce heat. Softly radiant, lightly brilliant.
Consisting of or arranged in laminae, thin plates or layers of metal or other material. Of the flow of a fluid: smooth and regular, not turbulent.
A four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, with folding front and rear hoods enabling it to travel open, half-open, or closed. Also landau carriage.
The fibrous pith of a reed stem. rare. Fine, soft hair or down, spec. that covering the human foetus; a covering resembling this.

The Trojan priest who warned against accepting the Trojan Horse from the Greeks and was subsequently killed by divine serpents. A statue of the ideal of Laocoön and his two sons, who were crushed to death by two sea serpents; also, a person resembling such a statue in action or appearance, a death-struggle.
A cutter, polisher, or engraver of gems or precious stones. Engraved on stone; suitable for inscriptions: dignified, concise.
Any of several mostly black and white plovers which occur in most temperate and tropical regions except N. America, esp. the peewit or green plover of Europe and Asia.

A thin narrow strip of wood, spec. one used to form a groundwork upon which to fasten the slates or tiles of a roof or the plaster of a wall or ceiling, or in the construction of lattice- or trelliswork and Venetian blinds. A slender or fragile thing or person.
A machine for holding horizontally and turning wood, ivory, metal, etc. for cutting into circular shapes.
Part of diseased; a leper. (noun + adj.) Lazarus- a person with leprosy; a beggar.
Sleight of hand; juggling, conjuring. Trickery, deception. An instance of legerdemain.

A court of record which the lords of certain manors were empowered to hold once or twice a year. The court's jurisdiction. A list of people designated as eligible for some office. (freq. short leet) A meeting of ways, a crossroads. Only in 2, 3 or 4-way leet.
A freckle, a pimple, spec. a small brown hyperpigmented patch of skin, usu. occurring on the face or hands, esp. of elderly people. Also the condition of having patches.
Of, pertaining to, or resembling a hare, harelike.
Inner bark; parchment; book (rare).

A piece of land worth a pound a year. To weigh. To oscillate like the beam of a balance; move from side to side or up and down. Oscillate or waver (between) one thing and another. Of a bird, etc.: be poised, balance itself. libratory (adj.), libration (n.)
In chemistry, a molecule, ion, atom, etc. capable of forming a coordination complex with a central (usu. a metal) atom.

A part of the body, considered with respect to its contour or outline; a distinctive physical feature. A part of the face viewed with respect to its outline; a facial feature, usually in plural. A line, delineation, diagram, outline, sketch, trace, and [illegible].
Penis (Sanskrit).
A kind of ornamentation produced by impressing upon porcelain or glass in a soft state.
Of or pertaining to the shore of the sea, a lake, etc.; existing or occurring on or adjacent to the shore.
Food, clothing, etc. being dispensed to servants, or horses. Clothing worn by servants of a particular employer, for recognition. Also badges or markings.

Impregnate with lye. (rare) Separate (a substance) into soluble and insoluble constituents by percolation of liquid, usu. water, leach. lixivium- a solution obtained by leaching, lye, spec. water containing alkaline salts leached from wood ashes. lixivious (adj.)
A heavy waterproof woolen cloth, a cloak made of this. An. A dark green color in which the cloth is often made. Made of this cloth.

Any of the heretics, from the 14th cent. on, to the Reformation, who were either followers of John Wyclif or held opinions similar to his, esp. on the necessity for the Church to aid people to live a life of evangelical poverty and imitate Jesus. A person who lolls; an idler. rare.
A pair of eyeglasses to be held in the hand; opera glasses.
(also lozel) A worthless person; a profligate, rake, scoundrel; in weaker sense a ragamuffin, a ne'er-do-well.
Frowning, scowling, angry-looking, gloomy, sullen. Of the clouds, sky, weather, circumstances etc.: gloomy, dark, threatening. Lurking, skulking.
Lewd, wanton, licentious. Slippery, smooth, slimy, oily. fig. Shifty, unstable, fickle, elusive.
A lamp, a lantern. A leguminous plant, Medicago sativa, cultivated for fodder, which bears blue to violet flowers and trifoliate leaves. Also called alfalfa.
Working or studying by artificial light at night. Also expression of one's thoughts in writing, esp. laboriously and elaborately. The act or product of lucubrating.
Characterized by, expressing, or causing mourning, mournful, doleful, dismal. (-iosity, -iously, -iousness)
Having the nature or qualities of a wolf.
(also lirche)- a game similar to backgammon.
Pertaining to or used in purification rites; purificatory. nu. Occurring every five years; quinquennial. lustrate (v), lustrative (adj.)
A form of madness in which a person believes himself or herself to be an animal (esp. a wolf) and behaves accordingly.
To spot, to stain, to soil; fig. defile, pollute. Spotted, stained, fig. defiled, polluted. Chiefly literary, in antithesis of immaculate.
An earthworm, a maggot. A whim.
The Muslim religion, Islam. Mohammedanism.
An elephant driver on the Indian subcontinent.

The state or condition of a maiden, virginity. Also, the hymen. A representation of the head or head and shoulders of the Virgin Mary, spec. (a) as an ornamental finish to the handle of a spoon (also: a spoon with such a handle). (b) Heraldry- as a charge on a shield, etc.
A fomenter of contention or trouble.
A dry, scabby eruption behind the knee in horses. (malender)
A little man, dwarf, pygmy. A small figure or statue of a man.

A religious system with Christian, Gnostic, and pagan elements, founded by the Persian Manes in the 3rd cent. AD and widespread in the Roman Empire and Asia until the 5th (surviving until the 13th), based on a supposed primeval conflict between light and darkness, and representing Satan as coeternal with God; dualism. (-istic, -an)

A poisonous and narcotic Mediterranean plant of the nightshade family with solitary purple or whitish flowers, which was formerly credited with magical and medicinal properties, due to its supposedly human-shaped root, reputed to shriek when taken from the ground. Something unwanted to be rooted up; a pestilential [illegible].
Wealth regarded as an idol or as an evil influence, from Mammon, the proper name of the devil of covetousness.
The edible substance described as miraculously supplied to the Israelites in the wilderness. Spiritual nourishment, esp. the Eucharist; something beneficial provided unexpectedly.

Excessive or affected adoption of a distinctive manner or method of treatment, specifically, a style of art which originated in Italy and preceded the baroque, characterized by stylistic exaggeration and distortion of figures, etc. A habitual peculiarity of style or manner.
A roof in which each face has two slopes, the lower one steeper than the upper; a curb roof.
A light scarf, frequently of black lace, worn over the head and shoulders, esp. by Spanish women. A small cape or mantle.
In music, each note being emphasized.
Inlaid work in wood, ivory, etc., esp. as used for the decoration of furniture.
In medieval Spain, a christianized Jew or Moor, esp. one professing conversion in order to avoid persecution.
Belonging to the early morning. A watchdog, a mastiff. (matin)
Of a celestial object: that rises above the horizon before sunrise. matutinal- of or pertaining to the morning, occurring or performed in the morning, early.
Grumble, mutter, growl. Move or act in a dreamy, idle, or inconsequent manner; dawdle. Fritter away (one's time, life, etc.). Say (something) in a dreamy and rambling manner.
Express sorrow (interjection). (Irish)
Inclined to sickness (obs). Having a nauseating, sickly, or insipid taste. Feebly sentimental, imbued with sickly or false sentiment.
An element of a culture or system of behavior that may be considered to be passed from one individual to another by nongenetic means, esp. imitation. memetic (adj.).
Habitual lying or deceiving.
A single tall upright monumental stone, esp. of prehistoric times.
The three membranes enveloping the brain and spinal cord, the dura mater, arachnoid, and pia mater.
Of, pertaining to, characteristic of, or befitting a prostitute, having the character of a prostitute. or. Showily but falsely attractive. meretrix- a prostitute.

A line of longitude, passing from pole to pole on the earth's surface. The point or period of highest development or perfection, full splendor, one's prime of life; zenith of the midday sun. A distinctive locality, situation, or characteristic, the tastes, habits, capacities, etc. of a particular set of people.
Chiefly anatomy. Pertaining to, situated in, or directed toward the middle line of a body; median. Also, situated mesially with respect to. mesially (adv.)
One's occupation or department of activity. Now usu. a field in which one has special skill or ability; one's forte.
A dunghill, manure heap, refuse-heap. A prehistoric refuse-heap of shells and bones and often also discarded artifacts. A receptacle for refuse, dustbin, the place where dustbins are kept.

An ancient homiletic commentary on a text from the Hebrew scriptures, characterized by non-literal interpretation and legendary illustration; also, the mode of exegesis characteristic of such a commentary. (plural: -im) (sic)
The spleen (now chiefly, that of a domestic animal). The semen of a male fish; the testes of a male fish. To fertilize a male fish. Of a male fish, to emit milt.

Imitation of another person's words or actions, or in representation of the real world in art, poetry, etc. The deliberate imitation of the behavior of one group of people by another as a factor in social change.
Of the color of cinnabar; vermilion.

A wrongful act or omission; spec. a misdemeanor or failure of duty by a public official. An offence similar to, but less serious than, treason or felony. Now, the crime of (deliberately) concealing one's knowledge of a treasonable act or a felony. The mistaking of one thing for another, a mistake.
A book containing the service of the Mass for the whole year, loosely, a Roman Catholic book of prayers; esp. when illuminated. Of or pertaining to the Mass. (adj.) (Also missal book).
A strong cold north-west wind which blows through the Rhône valley and southern France to the Mediterranean, mainly in winter.

(Also miter) an ecclesiastical head-dress worn by a bishop or abbot, in the shape of a pointed arch. A headband worn by women in ancient Greece. A high priest's turban. To bestow a mitre. A right-angled joint of wood. To join wood thusly.
A wool velvet, usu. of inferior quality, formerly used for clothing. Mockery. Inferior.
Wet, moisten, soil, bedaub. Now arch. Toil, work hard, drudge, freq. 'toil and moil'. A hornless cow or bull. Burrow (in). Lay obsolete. Move around in agitation or confusion; swirl, mill about.
From Hebrew molech, a Canaanite idol to whom children were sacrificed as burnt offerings. An object to which horrible sacrifices are made. A slow-moving spiny Australian lizard.

The Deity, God. (Monad) The number one, unity; a unit. (hist.) With reference to ancient Greek philosophy, in which the numbers were regarded as being generated from the unitary one. Leibniz: an indivisible unit of being (as a soul, an atom), an absolutely simple entity. A hypothetical simple organism assumed as the first term in the genealogy of living beings.
