In ancient Greece, an ode sung by a single voice, esp. by one of the actors in a tragedy, a mournful song or dirge. A poem in which a mourner bewails a person's death. Monotonous sound, monotony. A 17th-cent. musical style for one voice or instrument.

A metal tag, sometimes jewelled, at the end of a girdle's pendant. A substance enabling a dye or stain to become fixed. An adhesive compound for fixing gold leaf. A corrosive liquid or the like used in etching plate. Of sarcasm, etc.: caustic, incisive. Corrosion (rare). Pungent, biting. Of pain: acute, burning. mordancy- biting in speech, mordantly (adv.), mordacious (adj.), mordacity (n.).
Obedient, compliant, submissive (to).
A kind of helmet, without beaver or visor, worn by soldiers in the 16th and 17th centuries. A brown or black variety of quartz.
A crab-louse.

(Also morrice) A traditional English dance by groups of people in fancy costume (usu. representing legendary or symbolic figures) with ribbons and bells or sticks. To dance. slang, to be hanged; to go away rapidly or decamp (usu. with off). More fully nine men's morris, also merril- a game played on a board between two players, each with an equal number of pebbles, pegs or pins. Each counter used in this game.
Deadly.
A pout or pouting expression.
A travelling salesman who peddles all manner of goods, often including quack medicines.
Plain clothes worn by a person having the right to wear a uniform, esp. a military uniform.
A vertical bar dividing the lights in a window, esp. in Gothic architecture. Each of a series of ribs or columns on a rock face, wisely formed by folding. (-ed)

An obstinate adherent of old ways, in spite of clear evidence of their error; an ignorant and bigoted opponent of reform. A traditional custom or notion obstinately adhered to, although shown to be unreasonable.

A document (as a title deed, charter, etc.) preserved as evidence of rights or privileges (usu. in pl.). In pl. archives. In pl. Things with which a person or place is provided, furnishings. Anything serving as a defense or protection (rare).
Plague, pestilence, esp. the potato blight during the Irish famine in the mid 19th century. An infectious disease of livestock. Death, mortality, esp. by plague or pestilence.
Individual who unhesitatingly obeys orders. From the warriors who accompanied Achilles.

(The title of) any of certain Muslim officials acting as deputy governors of provinces or districts in the Mughal Empire; a governor of an Indian town or district. A person of great wealth or (formerly) high rank; spec. a person returning from India with a large fortune acquired there; a wealthy, luxury-loving person.
Consisting of or resembling nacre, mother-of-pearl; pearly.
Orig. liquid petroleum. Now, any mixture of volatile flammable liquid distillation products used esp. as solvents and in gasoline.
The art of prediction by supposed communication with the dead; magic, enchantment, conjuration.
Intense burning or stabbing pain, typically along the line of a nerve, esp. in the face.
Wink, blink. Also nictitate.
(Pl. of nitery)- Night clubs. Nitery- An impulse.
A guilty person, a criminal. The guilty as a class. Harmful, injurious, hurtful. Guilty, criminal. nocency: guilt.
A small drinking vessel; a mug, a cup. A small quantity of alcoholic liquor; usu. a quarter of a pint; a small drink of spirits.
(Also Noax) a fool, a simpleton.
A local ruler or governor. (rare) The governor of an ancient Egyptian nome. The senior administrator or (formerly) governor of a modern Greek nomarchy.

The ninth day (by inclusive reckoning) before the Ides in the ancient Roman calendar, the 7th of March, May, July, and October, and the 5th of the other months. The fifth of the daytime canonical hours of prayer, orig. appointed for the ninth hour of the day (about 3pm), the office appointed for this hour.
The scarlet lychnis. Nonesuch chest- a type of wooden chest of the 16th and 17th centuries, inlaid with stylized architectural designs supposedly representing Henry VIII's Nonsuch Palace.

The sphere or stage of evolutionary development characterized by (the emergence or dominance of) consciousness, the mind, and interpersonal relationships (freq. with reference to the writings of Teilhard de Chardin). (20th century Jesuit philosopher, censured by Roman Catholic church.)
In Greek philosophy, intuitive apprehension, intelligence; mind, intellect. Common sense, practical intelligence, gumption.
A devotion consisting of special prayers or services on nine successive days.
Night personified.
Trifling, of no value or importance, worthless. E17. Not valid, inoperative, useless, futile. E19.
A rapid, involuntary, usually lateral, oscillation of the eyeball.

A person dedicated to monastic or religious life or work; spec (a) a child offered to a monastery, to be brought up, (b) a lay person attached to a religious community without taking vows, (c) a member of a secular community devoted to some special work. Flattened at the poles. oblation- offering something to God or a god; the offering of the bread and wine in the Eucharist. A sacrifice, oblata (old) debts or gifts to a monarch.
Noisy, vociferous, characterized by clamorous opposition. Turbulent, unruly, noisily resisting control, advice, etc.
Thrust a thing forward forcibly or without invitation, press or impose a matter, person, etc. (on). Eject, force out.
Possessing (good) sight, sharp-eyed, observant. In botany, having eyelike spots or holes resembling eyes; ocellate.
The fact or state of being hated; general or widespread unpopularity or approbation. Odeum- A building for the performance of vocal and instrumental music, esp. among the ancient Greeks and Romans.
A work of art, music, literature, etc.; the whole body of work produced by an artist, composer, etc.
In Irish history, an expert in an art or branch of learning; a learned man of a rank corresponding to that of a university professor. (also ollav)
Anglo-Irish (derog.) a foolish person. (also omad (haun and other vars.))
The condition of being all, allness. omniana- notes or scraps of information about all kinds of things.
Masturbation. Coitus interruptus.
The science or study of being; that part of metaphysics which relates to the nature or essence of being or existence.
Showing varying colors like an opal; having a milky iridescence.
An occasion or cause of reproach, shameful conduct, something that brings disgrace; disgrace attached to conduct considered shameful; shame. (-ate, -ious, -y)
Fight against; attack; assault. Assail or oppose with words, action, etc.; esp. call into question, dispute the truth of.
Filth, dirt, excrement, dung. Moral defilement, corruption, obscene language, an obscene action.
A platform over the hold of a ship forming the lowest deck, esp. in a ship of more than three decks. (also orlop deck).

Orig. gold or gold leaf prepared for gilding brass, bronze, etc. Later, gilded bronze or a gold-colored alloy of copper, zinc, and tin used to decorate furniture, make ornaments, etc.; articles made of or decorated with this.
Of a voice, utterance, etc.: full, round, imposing, clear, resonant. Of writing, style of expression, etc.: inflated, pretentious.
Usu. pl. (orts), fragments of food left over from a meal; fodder left by cattle, refuse scraps. Anything left over, remains.

Kiss. Of a curve or surface: touch (another curve or surface) without crossing, so as to have a common tangent. Of two curves or surfaces: have a common tangent. Come into close contact or union; come together.
(A shoot of) any of several willows with tough plant branches used in basket-work.
(Made of) a kind of coarse linen (later cotton) used for pillowcases, sacks, etc. orig. from Osnabrück.
Having no practical result, futile. Having no practical function, superfluous. At leisure, at rest, idle; indolent.
Beyond the bounds of what is usual or proper, eccentric, unusual, out-of-the-way.
Each of the Twelve bravest and most famous warriors of Charlemagne's court. Also, a knight errant, a champion.

Paper, parchment, etc. prepared for writing on and wiping out, like a slate; or, where the original writing has been effaced to make way for other writing; a monumental brass slab turned and re-engraved on the reverse side. (also adj.; verb trans: palimpsest manuscript; make into a palimpsest) (palimpsestic)

A fence of pales or iron railings fixed in the ground, forming an enclosure or defense; a light fence or trellis on which trees or shrubs are trained; a row of trees or shrubs. Fortifying: a close hedge, a strong pointed stick fixed deeply in the ground with others in a close row, as a defense; a thing like a row of stakes; a line of high cliffs; a parallel region of cells.
A straw mattress made with sacking or other strong material.
Make an examination of by the sense of touch, esp. for medical purposes.
A public speech or text in praise of someone or something; a laudatory discourse; eulogy. (on).
Difference or change in the apparent position or direction of an object as seen from two different points. The fact of seeing wrongly or in a distorted way (rare).
A rope arranged like a sling for raising or lowering heavy objects. To raise or lower (esp. casks or cylindrical objects) with a parbuckle.
Perilous, dangerous. Awkward, precarious; risky to deal with. Keen, shrewd, cunning, malicious, wicked. Also, extraordinary, excessive. In an excessive manner.
A sliding band of rope or metal attaching a yard or boom to a mast while allowing it vertical movement.

The careful or sparing use of money or other material resources; stinginess, niggardliness. Economy in the use of immaterial things; spec. the principle that organisms tend towards economy of action in learning or fulfilling needs. Occam's razor- no more assumptions should be made than are necessary (law of parsimony).
A level space in a garden occupied by an ornamental arrangement of flower beds. A level space on which a house or village stands.
The action of giving birth to young; childbirth. Parturient- about to give birth, ready to produce something. Parturiate- produce young, give birth.

(Fem. -ue) A person of humble origin who has gained wealth, position, and risen in society, esp. one regarded as unfitted for the position achieved in this way, or lacking the accomplishments appropriate to it; an upstart.
The notional branch of knowledge that deals with the realm additional to metaphysics; a concept introduced by Alfred Jarry (1873-1907), French writer and dramatist of the absurd.

A usu. green film produced by oxidation on the surface of old bronze, coins, flint, etc. A gloss or sheen on wooden furniture produced by age, polishing, etc. An acquired change in the appearance of a surface, esp. one suggestive of age. (ed)

Of, pertaining to, resembling, or characteristic of a peacock. Resembling the neck or tail of a peacock in coloring. An iridescent tarnish found on some ores and metals. pavonian- pertaining to, or resembling a peacock.
Embezzlement, esp. of public money or property by an official. An instance of this.
Consisting of money, exacted in money. Of an offence: entailing a money penalty or fine. Of or pertaining to money.
Goddess of volcanoes in Hawaiian mythology.
Stolen goods, booty. Property, possessions. Money, riches. Now esp. dishonestly acquired wealth.
A small or thin skin; a fine sheet or layer covering a surface or (occas.) enclosing a cavity; a membrane, a cuticle, a film.
The protective gods of a Roman household, esp. of its storeroom; household gods. lares and penates- the home (large Roman household or ancestral god. In pl. the protective gods of a house.)
(also panel) Brown unpurified sugar from the Antilles (also panell, pannel, paneel, panela).

The partially shaded outer region of a shadow (contrasted with the umbra) when the light comes from a source of some size; esp. that of the shadow cast by the moon or the earth in an eclipse; the lighter periphery of a sunspot; any partial shade or shadow round a thing; a surrounding area of uncertain extent.
Destitution, indigence. A lack, dearth, or scarcity of something.

A person who or thing which perceives; spec. one who perceives something outside the range of the senses, a person with extrasensory perception. That perceives or is capable of perceiving, conscious, perceptive, discerning. (percipience, -cy, -tly)
A falcon. Foreign, outlandish, strange, imported from abroad. Formerly also, extraneous to the matter at hand. Travelling, wandering. Formerly also, on a pilgrimage.
Deceitful breach of faith or betrayal of trust, esp. the profession of faith or friendship in order to deceive or betray.
Olivine (chrysolite), esp. as used as gem; an olive-colored shade of green.

A member of the sect of philosophers who held the doctrines of Aristotle; also adj. of the sect and system of philosophy of Aristotle. A person who walks or travels about; (chiefly joc.) an itinerant dealer or trader; a peripatetic teacher. E17.
A row of columns surrounding a building, court, cloister, etc., the court etc. surrounded by the columns. E17. The columned porch of a church or other large building, a pillared veranda.
Light banter or raillery, frivolous talk. (Persifleur- one who indulges in persiflage.)

Having a clear understanding; perceptive, discerning. Seeing clearly (arch.) Perspicuous (adj.) Perspicuity- transparency, translucence. Clearness of statement or exposition, lucidity. Distinctness to the sight, conspicuousness. Discernment, perspicacity. Formerly also keenness of sight.
A vaginal suppository used to treat infection or as a contraceptive.
Sea birds with mainly black (or brown) and white plumage and usually a hooked bill; some of which feed while seeming to walk on the sea.

A member of a sect within Judaism between the 2nd cent. BC and the time of Jesus who observed strictly the tradition of the elders as well as the written Mosaic law, as they interpreted it. A person of the (Pharisaic) spirit or disposition attributed to the Pharisees in the New Testament; a hypocrite, a self-righteous person.

The collecting and study of postage stamps or other devices used for prepayment of postal charges. Postage stamps collectively. philatelic(al) (adj.), philatelic (adj.), philatelist (n.), philatelism (n.).

A member of a foreign militaristic people who in biblical times occupied the southern coast of Palestine and were hostile to the Israelites. An antagonist, an enemy, a debauched or drunken person, aesthetically unsophisticated. An uneducated or unenlightened person, a person indifferent or hostile to culture, or whose interests and tastes are commonplace and material.
A spoken or written diatribe against; passionately disliked person, idea, or course of action.

Love of learning and literature; the branch of knowledge that deals with the linguistic, historical, interpretive, and critical aspects of literature, literary or classical scholarship. The branch of knowledge that deals with the structure, historical development, and relationships of a language or languages.
A philosophical statement, theorem, or axiom; a demonstration or conclusion in philosophy.
The supreme object of alchemy, a substance supposed to change any metal into gold or silver and (according to some) to cure all diseases and prolong life indefinitely. A universal cure or solution.

(Also philtre) A potion, drug, or (occas.) charm, supposed to attract sexual attention, esp. to a particular person; a love potion. Gen. any allegedly magic potion or drug. To charm or bewitch with a philter.
(Also phizog) A person's face, a facial expression.
An acid obtained by Chevreul in 1817, from porpoise or dolphin-oil, originally called delphimic and subsequently identified with valeric acid.
A region at the foot of a mountain or mountain range. (noun + adj.)
A typical character in French pantomime. Now also a musical entertainer with a whitened face and a loose white costume.
Esp. a light saddle for a woman, a pad attached to the back of a saddle for an additional rider or luggage, or a seat for a passenger behind the rider of a motorcycle. Equip with a pillion.

A small outgrowth near the third ventricle of the brain, which has an endocrine function, in some vertebrates forming a light-sensitive median eye (pineal eye) involved in control of circadian rhythms, and in others secreting melatonin.

A small light vessel, usu. two-masted and schooner-rigged, often used for communicating between a senior officer's ship and other vessels under his command. A small boat (orig. eight-oared, now usu. motor-driven) forming part of the equipment of a warship or other larger vessel. A woman; spec. a mistress, a prostitute.

(Also piquante) Sharp or stinging to the feelings; severe, bitter. Of food etc.: agreeably pungent, sharp tasting, spicy; savory, appetizing. Pleasantly stimulating to the mind, racy, spicy; fascinating, charming. Something sharp and pointed. Also a spicy dish.

A quarrel or feeling of enmity between two or more. Resentment at a slight or injury, esp. to pride. Stimulate or provoke by arousing jealousy. Wound the pride of, irritate, or offend. Card game: a score, pointed end of a collar, bullet.
A mountain range east of the River Jordan, from where Moses was allowed to view the promised land. (with sight or view) a faint view or glimpse of something unobtainable or distant.
A European flatfish, which is brown with orange spots and a white underside, and is an important food fish. Fluke, American plaice. The flesh of these fish.
An accusation to a court, a charge. A statement of wrong, injury, or injustice; a complaint. The action or an act of plaining; lamentation. Make complaint; cover or fill with complaints.
Esp. of the sound of the sea, waves, etc.: reverberating, mournfully resonant. Loud sounding, strident, plaintive, sad.

A shallow piece of standing water, a marshy pool, a puddle, mersh, mire. The sound produced by water or other liquid striking something or being struck; a splash. A heavy fall of rain. Bend down and interweave to form a hedge or fence. Interlace in a trellis.

Complete, entire, perfect, not deficient in any clause or respect; absolute, unqualified. Having all the members of an assembly, etc. present, fully constituted or attended. Of, presented to, or taking place at a full session. In law, a complete or ordinary proceeding. Possessing full powers or authority. (Crete) plenary indulgence- a complete remission of temporal punishment for sin in Roman Catholicism.

The condition of being absolutely full in quantity, measure, or degree; completeness, perfection. Corporative fullness, plentifuliness, abundance. In heraldry, fullness of the moon. Abundance or excess of blood or humors; fullness, affluence, full supply.

A structure consisting of a bundle of minute closely interwoven and intercommunicating fibers or tubes; a network of nerve fibers or blood vessels, usu. with specifying word. Any intertwined or interwoven mass, an intricate arrangement or collection of things; a such a network.

A marking on a ship's side indicating the legal limit of the ship's submersion when loaded with cargo under various sea conditions. A rubber-soled canvas leisure or sports shoe. (Plimsoll line, Plimsoll mark, Plimsoll's mark)
Plumpness.

Measure the depth of water with a plumb (a heavy ball attached to a line); determine a depth; get to the bottom of, explore or experience the emotional depths. Weight with lead. Vertically, perpendicularly, straight down. Fall vertically. Completely, exactly, precisely; directly.
A paltry or inferior poet, a writer of poor or trashy verse. us. poetast (v). E20.
A controversial argument or discussion; argumentation against some opinion, doctrine, etc., aggressive controversy. Esp. in theology.

A slow dance of Polish origin, consisting mainly of a march or procession; the music for this dance. A Polish dress; a Polish dish; a Polish rug or carpet. A type of carpet made in Persia in the 16th and 17th centuries using silver and gold warp threads.
The calcined ashes of a plant, brought from the eastern Mediterranean region and Syria, and used in glassmaking.
A person of much or varied learning, a person acquainted with various subjects of study, a great scholar.
A small, slim dagger. Stab with a small dagger; esp. to death.
A hard rock quarried in ancient Egypt, having white or red crystals in a red groundmass; any red or purple stone taking a high polish.

A strong barrier in the form of a grating of wooden or iron bars, usu. suspended by chains above the gateway of a fortress, etc., and able to be quickly released to slide down vertical grooves in the sides of the gateway and secure the entrance. A figure of a portcullis, as ornament or heraldic charge. A silver halfpenny issued in the reign of Queen Eliz. I, with a portcullis on one side.
A curtain hung over a door or doorway, as a screen or for ornament, or to prevent drafts.

A marginal note or comment on a text, esp. Scripture; a series of such comments, a commentary, spec. an expository discourse or homily on a Gospel or Epistle, to be read in a church service. Annotate, inscribe with marginal notes.

The practice or action of a technical subject or art, as opposed to the theory of it. Habitual action, accepted practice, custom. In Marxism, the willed action by which a theory or philosophy becomes a practical social activity.

The portion of the revenues of a cathedral or collegiate church formerly granted to a canon or member of the chapter, as his stipend. The property from which such a stipend was derived, the tenure of this as a benefice. prebendary- a canon receiving a prebend or of the old foundation.
A summary or abstract, esp. of a text or speech. The action or practice of précis-writing. Make a précis of, summarize.
The foreskin. Also, the fold of skin surrounding the clitoris. The state of uncircumcision.

Persistent erection of the penis, commonly due to a blood clot in the erectile tissue. = Priapus (A statue or image of the god Priapus, esp. with large genitals). Lewdness, licentiousness. Priapist- worshipper of Priapus; lecher.
Anglo-Irish diminutive of priest.
A gambling card-game, fashionable in the 16th and 17th centuries, in which each player was dealt four cards.
Integrity, uprightness of character, conscientiousness, honesty, sincerity.
Having a projecting jaw, (of jaws) prominent, protruding. (-thism, -thy, -thously)
Of long duration, lengthy, protracted, esp. (of speech, writing, a speaker, etc.) verbose, long-winded. prolixious (adj.), prolixity (n.), prolixly (adv.), prolixness (n.).
An introductory or preliminary course of study in an art or science.

Propitious- Well disposed, favorably inclined, (of an omen) good, boding well, favorable, timely, opportune. Propitiate- Make propitious or favorably inclined; appease, conciliate, placate. Propitiatory- a propitiation; offering of atonement. (-tion, -tily, -tible, -tingly, -tive, -tor)

The performance area between the background and the orchestra of a theater, the stage. en. The part of the stage of a modern theater between the curtain or drop-scene and the auditorium, often including the curtain itself and the enclosing arch. The front; the foreground. The theater as a profession, dramatic art. (rare)

The first part of a play, in which the characters and subject are introduced, preceding epitasis and catastrophe. en. The first or introductory clause in a sentence, esp. the clause expressing the condition in a conditional sentence. uk. Something which is put forward; a proposition, a maxim (rare).
Of, pertaining to, or characteristic of the god Proteus of classical mythology, taking or existing in many forms, changing, varying, versatile, unpredictable, following no obvious pattern.
Food, provisions, esp. dry food for horses; animal fodder.

The Book of Psalms. A translation or particular version (prose or metrical) of the Book of Psalms, esp. one appointed to be used in a church. A copy or a volume containing the Psalms, esp. one for liturgical or devotional use. A selection from, or portion of, the Psalms for a particular service or purpose. Any of various old Irish chronicles in verse.

Any of several N. American plants from which pigments are obtained, esp. (more fully red puccoon) the bloodroot, and (more fully, hoary puccoon) Lithospermum canescens. Bloodroot is a.k.a. Sanguinaria canadensis. Both yield a red dye. Also (more fully yellow puccoon) golden seal, Hydrastis canadensis, which yields a yellow dye.
The state or condition of being a girl, maidenhood, virginity.
Having a keen sense of shame, modest, chaste. us. Pudenda. (rare). us. pudicity- modesty, chastity. M. pudor- due sense of shame, bashfulness, modesty. us. pudical (adj.)
Having great authority or influence, mighty, strong, powerful. Puissance- strength; a showjumping competition for horses; an armed force, a crowd of people.
Beauty. (-udinous)
Flea-infested, flea-bitten, resembling a flea bite.
A young hen between the ages of chicken and mature fowl, spec. from point-of-lay until first moult.
Sprout, bud, germinate, propagate by budding. Also, swarm, multiply, breed prolifically. Develop, spring up, come to life. Teem, swarm, abound (with).

A large cask for liquids, fish, etc. Used as a measure. A piece of timber, esp. a short upright piece of timber used to stiffen longer timbers or to support a load; a strut, a post supporting a roof in a coalmine. Formerly also, a short post. A heavy piece of rough timber used for flooring and rough building, railroad track, or corduroy road. A pointed or piercing instrument, a dagger; a tool for piercing, punching, stamping, etc.
Any of a class of sacred works in Sanskrit, chiefly in verse, containing the mythology and traditional lore of the Hindus.
Having impaired or defective vision, dim-sighted. Of a thing: dimly lit. Having imperfect perception or discernment, obtuse; dull, dim-witted. Impair the sight or perception of, make purblind.

A tract of land on the border of a forest, esp. one formerly included within the forest boundaries and still partly subject to the forest laws. An outlying district of a city or town, a suburb. Also, a squalid or disreputable street or quarter. us. A place where a person has a right to range at large.
Of a person: lacking in courage, timid, cowardly, mean-spirited. Of a quality, action, etc.: resulting from or displaying meanness of spirit or a lack of courage. en.
That is believed to be such; reputed, supposed. Putanism- the occupation of a prostitute, prostitution.
In the Middle Ages, the higher division of a course of study of seven sciences, comprising arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, and music.
A leaf or flower consisting of four (usu. rounded) leaflets or petals radiating from a common center; a representation or imitation of this, esp. as a charge in heraldry, and in architecture.
The inherent nature or essence of a person or thing, that which constitutes a person or thing. A nicety in argument; a quibble; the ability or tendency to use quiddities in argument.
Motionless, inert, dormant. A silent consonant.
A galley, probably having five rowers to each bank of oars.
(also kintal, kentle) Orig., a weight of one hundred pounds. Later, a hundredweight. Now, a weight of 100 kilograms.

Daily, of or pertaining to every day. (of a fever, etc.) recurring every day. Of a person: performing some act or sustaining some characteristic daily. Ordinary, everyday, commonplace, trivial. A daily allowance or portion. (-ly)

Red ochre, ruddle. Paint or mark with ruddle, color coarsely with red or rouge. The rail of a cart. (rare) A wooden bar with upright pegs for keeping the threads of the warp in place as it is wound upon the beam.
A medieval Jewish merchant who traded between southern France and China, keeping the ancient Roman and Silk Road trade routes open from approx. AD 500-1000.
The embryonic root in a seedling plant. A minute branch of a nerve, vein, etc.
Carefully sought out, rare, exotic, far-fetched, obscure. recherche du temps perdu- 'in search of the lost time,' a novel by Proust.
A person who relapses, esp. habitually into crime.
Of study, discussion, etc.: consisting in or relating to little-known or profound knowledge. Of a writer or literary style: employing abstruse or obscure allusions or references.
The state or fact of breaking out afresh, a recurrence, esp. of a disease, a wound, or something unpleasant. A revival or rediscovery of something good or valuable. (more recently)
Reclining, leaning, lying down. A bicycle ridden in a reclining position. A megalithic stone lying (intentionally) on the ground. recumbency, recumbently.
Formidable, to be feared. Also, (of a person) commanding respect.
Shining with a brilliant light, radiant, gleaming.
Convert a concept, etc. mentally into a thing; materialize.

A transfer or surrender of property, the action of remitting money, a remittance. A shelter for a carriage, a coach-house. A hired carriage of a better class than hackney. A second thrust in fencing while still lunging. To replace, put back (in or into) a place, state, etc.; resort again (into); send back (to). Surrender or make over (a right, property, etc.). To remise in fencing.
Being reborn, reviving, springing up afresh. A person who takes part in a renaissance.

An index, a catalogue, a calendar. A store, a repository, esp. of retrievable examples or information. In. A repertoire. The performance of plays, operas, ballets, etc. by a company at regular short intervals. A theatrical, operatic, or ballet company that performs works from a repertoire.

The action or an act of repining. To cause trouble to. (rare) To feel or express regretful dissatisfaction; fret, complain (foll. by against, at, or that). To long discontentedly (for). To regard with regretful dissatisfaction, complain at.
Raising metalwork into ornamental relief by pounding the opposite side. Metalwork fashioned by repoussé.
An object in the foreground of a painting serving to emphasize the principal figure or scene.
A person who has returned, esp. (noun) supposedly from the dead, a ghost. Returned, esp. supposedly from the dead. (adj.)

A member of a class of retainers who also used as irregular troops; a menial, a serf. merit. A low-born or worthless person, a knave, a wretch. A wicked, dissolute, or licentious person. A person using offensively impious or lewd language; an irreverent or scurrilous person. Lewd, coarse, scurrilous, irreverent, impious.
Ribbon, in heraldry (also ribband).
Of, pertaining to, situated on, or inhabiting the banks of a river, riverine. A riparian proprietor. ripicolous- inhabiting or frequenting riverbanks.
A unit of exposure to X- or gamma radiation.
A novel in which actual people or events appear under fictitious names. Literally, novel with a key.
A piece of music with a recurring leading theme, often as the final movement of a concerto, sonata, etc. A game of chance played with balls on a table.

A cross as an instrument of execution. The Cross on which Jesus suffered, the cross as the symbol of the Christian faith. A crucifix, esp. one above a rood-screen (separating the nave from the chancel). A former measure of area for land, later standardized at a quarter of an acre, equal to 40 square perches.

A method of gravure printing using a rotary press, esp. used for long print runs of magazines, stamps, etc., a sheet or section of a magazine printed by this method. Gravure= Photogravure= Photographically transferring an image to a plate for intaglio printing.
A mixture of melted fat (esp. butter) and flour used as a thickener in making sauces, etc.
Inclined to redness; red. Of the face, complexion, etc.: reddish, flushed, highly colored, esp. as the result of good living, a person having such a complexion.

A written or printed text in distinctive (esp. red) lettering, esp. (a) a chapter or section heading, (b) a liturgical direction for a divine service, (c) a calendar of saints, (d) a statute or section of a legal code, (e) a note introducing an exam paper, etc. A designation, category, injunction, general rule, established custom. (-al, -ally, -ian, -ion)
An ill-natured or cantankerous woman, a hag. (noun + adj.)

The space between a bed and the wall; the part of a bed next to the wall. A ladies' bedroom used to hold fashionable morning receptions, a reception held in such a room (17th & 18th cent. France). In France: a small street, a lane; an alley.
Reddish-brown, rust-colored. Either of two reddish-brown moths.
Boisterous, noisy, unruly, turbulent, rough.

Of or pertaining to a priest or the priesthood; priestly. Of a doctrine, etc.: ascribing sacrificial functions and supernatural functions to ordained priests; claiming excessive authority for the priesthood.
The supreme chief of some N. American Indians. E17. A prominent member of a society, etc., a political leader.
A religious ceremony or act imparting spiritual grace to the participants, esp. in the Catholic and Orthodox churches, esp. baptism and Eucharist.
A tree-sized branching cactus found in desert regions of Mexico and the south-western U.S.
A Russian tea urn, with an internal heating device to keep the water at boiling point.
Wise. Now only ironic or literary. Having knowledge of, aware of. Rare. Of modern man, Homo sapiens. A wise man, a sage. Now only joc.
A provincial governor in ancient Persia. A subordinate ruler, esp. a tyrannic one. Satrapy- a province ruled by a satrap.
A spiritual discourse, a sacred gathering, in Indian philosophy (Sanskrit).
The festival of Saturn, held in mid-December and characterized by general unrestrained merrymaking, the precursor of Christmas. A period of unrestrained tumult and revelry, an orgy. (-ian)
Born under or affected by the influence of the planet Saturn, now usually, of a cold, sluggish, and gloomy temperament, of dark and grim appearance.
A leap, a jump, spec. by a horse. A waterfall, a rapid. N.Amer. E17.

Marked by suggestive of, or showing an interest in scandal or salacious detail; indecent, risqué. Full of obstacles; a subject or situation difficult to deal with and requiring tactful handling. Rough to the touch, esp. of plants.
The action of climbing up. (rare) The metrical scanning of verse, the division of a verse into metrical feet.
Malicious enjoyment of another's misfortune.

The slag or dross remaining after the smelting out of a metal from its ore. Rough masses resembling clinker, formed by the cooling of volcanic ejecta, and of a light aerated texture. scoriaceous (adj.), scoriform (adj.), scoriac (adj.).
Fornication. scortatory- of, pertaining to, or consisting in fornication or lewd behavior.
Open-weave fabric (thin canvas or loosely woven cotton or linen) used chiefly for upholstery and in the building trades.
To decorate (bone, ivory, shells, etc.) with carved or colored designs, as a craft or pastime originally practiced by sailors during long voyages. An item of work produced in this way.
Of a person, literature, etc.: morally corrupt. Caused by, resembling, or affected by scrofula (tuberculosis of the lymph nodes).

A domestic servant of the lowest rank in a household, employed to wash dishes and perform other menial kitchen tasks. Scullery: A small kitchen or attached room for dishwashing and other dirty household work.

Orig. an opening in a ship's side on a level with the deck to allow water to run away. Usu. in plural. A drainage ditch. A prostitute, derog. a woman. Kill, esp. in an ambush. Defeat, ruin, thwart, put an end to. Sink (a ship) deliberately, scuttle.

Any condition or disease in people or animals characterized by the production of loose scales or flaky skin. The scales or flakes of epidermis that are continually cast off as fresh skin forms below, esp. such scales present in abnormally large numbers, esp. in seborrhoeic conditions of the scalp; dandruff. Any incrustation or flaky or scaly deposit. A miser, skintflint, esp. an employer, or cheap laborer.

Narrow-leaved coarse plants of marshes and watersides, sometimes used for thatching. The characteristic greenish- (or reddish-) brown shade of sedge. An artificial fishing lure imitating a caddis fly.
Painstaking, persevering, diligent, assiduous, persistent, (of an action) deliberately and consciously continued.

Of, pertaining to, or derived from the moon (also selenian). Of or containing selenium, a non-metallic chemical element characterized by a strong photoelectric effect. Selenite- a supposed inhabitant of the moon.
Growing old, elderly, aging. (-ce, -senesce)
The official responsible for the management of a medieval great house or estate; steward, major-domo. The governor of a city, county, province, etc. A cathedral official.

Full of meaning, intelligence, or wisdom. Of language, style, etc.: filled with pointed maxims, aphoristic, pithy, affectedly or pompously formal, turgid. A person given to the use of maxims, having a concise effective style, prone to pompous moralizing or bombastic formality.
A native of the Indian subcontinent employed as a soldier, under European, esp. British, military discipline.

(Pl. of seraph) In Christian theology, a member of the first and highest order of the ninefold celestial hierarchy, ranking directly above the cherubim, and gifted with love and associated with light, ardor, and purity (usu. in pl.). Also, a conventional representation of such a being, esp. as a human face or figure with six wings. Also, a person distinguished for seraphic qualities.

Dried up, withered, esp. from old age. A catch of a gunlock which engages to keep the hammer at half cock or full cock; a claw or talon. A series of plant communities (or occas. animals), each naturally succeeding the previous one.

A person responsible for looking after a church, its contents, and the churchyard, frequently acting as bell-ringer and gravedigger. Sextry= Sacristy- a room in a religious house or church for keeping the vestments, sacred vessels, etc., and used by a celebrant preparing for a service.
A kind of untanned leather with a rough granular surface, frequently dyed green, an imitation of this. The skin of various sharks, rays, etc. Used for polishing.
(Also chaco) French, Hungarian and German cylindrical military hat with a peak and a plume or pompom.
A large heavy boat fitted with one or more masts and carrying fore-and-aft or lug sails and sometimes furnished with guns. A boat for use in shallow waters, a dinghy.
An old form of chess, which came from India. The second known variant of chess, developed by changing the first variant, Chaturanga.

A word used as a test for detecting people from another district or country by their pronunciation; a word or sound very difficult for foreigners to pronounce correctly. A peculiarity of pronunciation in one area. A long-standing idea held unreflectingly by a group, class, etc. A slogan or truism.

Of or pertaining to the stars. Starlike, lustrous, bright (rare). Of a period of time: determined or measured with reference to the apparent motion of the stars; of planetary or lunar motion: relative to the stars. (-ly)
Crescent-shaped, semicircular. Having a double curve like the letter S. A curve or graph having a steep central portion which flattens out at top and bottom.
Fodder preserved by pressure in a silo. Also, storage in a silo.
(Also simpkin) Urdu for champagne.
An ecclesiastical benefice without cure of souls. A position or office requiring little or no work, esp. one yielding profit or honor. Holding a sinecure.
David Alfaro Siqueiros- Mexican painter of protest murals.
Fiber from the leaves of several Mexican agaves, used for cordage, matting, etc.; any of the plants producing this fiber.

In Cambridge University, and at Trinity College, Dublin, an undergraduate receiving an allowance from the college to enable him or her to study, and formerly required to perform certain menial duties.
A length of thread or yarn, loosely coiled and knotted, esp. into a figure eight. A tangle, a confusion. A flight of wild fowl, esp. geese or swans.
Rascal, scoundrel, villain (S. Africa). Villainous, untrustworthy, wily, bad-tempered.
Strike, slap, smack, drive or rout with blows; kick violently. Skip, walk, or run quickly. (n.) (-er, -ing)
(also snaphance) An early form of flintlock, used in muskets and pistols, the hammer of this. A musket, gun, etc. fitted with a flintlock of this kind, used in the 16th and 17th centuries.
Catch with a noose; snare. A snare, a noose.
Of a person: self-styled, would-be. Of a thing: so-called; pretended.
Meticulously dressed, prepared, or arranged; well-groomed.
A sum of money or other compensation given to a person to make up for loss, inconvenience, injured feelings, etc., spec. in law, such an amount awarded to a litigant over and above the actual loss.

Characterized by or showing anxiety, care, or concern. Troubled, anxious, or deeply concerned on some specified account (about, for, of); apprehensive, uneasy. Particularly careful or attentive, taking the utmost care, anxious, eager, or desirous to do something. (-ly, -ness)
In philosophy, the view or theory that the self really exists or can be known. Also, isolation, self-centeredness, selfishness. (-sistic, -sistically, -sist, -sismal)
Of, pertaining to, or affecting the body, esp. as distinct from the mind; bodily, corporeal, physical. Soma- the body in contrast to the mind or the soul (opp. psyche).
A musical composition for one or two instruments, one usu. being the piano, usu. in several movements, of two, four, and sometimes others in sonata form (a composition with three main sections).

In ancient Greece, a scholar, teacher; spec. a paid teacher of philosophy and rhetoric, esp. one associated with specious reasoning and moral scepticism; (now rare) a wise or learned person. Now, a person using clever but fallacious arguments; a specious reasoner, a casuist.
Inducing or tending to produce sleep; very tedious or boring. Resembling sleep or sleepiness. Of a person: drowsy, sleepy, somnolent. A drug, influence, etc., which induces sleep.
The action or an act of divining or deciding something by casting lots. Also, sorcery, magic. A person who practices sortilege. (rare) sortileger (n.), sortilegious (adj.), sortilegy (n.).

A maidservant or lady's maid as a character in a play or opera, esp. one of a pert or coquettish character; an actress or singer playing the role of a pert or coquettish female in any light entertainment.
A usu. gentle rushing or murmuring sound as of wind, water, etc. A hypocritical or overly pious manner of speaking, esp. in preaching or praying. A deep sigh or breath.

A space between timbers supporting a building; later, the almost triangular space between one side of the outer curve of an arch and the rectangle formed by the mouldings enclosing it, esp. a wall and ceiling, freq. filled in with ornamental work; also the space between the shoulders of adjoining arches and the ceiling, moulding, etc. above; spaces between the central field and border of an ornamental.
A kind of small harpsichord with the strings set obliquely to the keyboard, popular esp. in the 18th century. (spinet piano) A thicket, a spinney.

A person with a disease of the spleen. A peevish or ill-humored person. A medicine for diseases of the spleen. Pertaining to the spleen. Affected with melancholia or hypochondria. Irritable, peevish, ill-tempered, testy.
In prosody, a metrical foot consisting of two long or (in English etc.) two stressed syllables; a verse composed of or containing such feet.
The track, trail, or scent of a person or animal, esp. the footprints of a wild animal hunted as game. To follow a trail of spoor.
Esp. of breathing: characterized by or of the nature of stertor; sounding like snoring; heavy. stertor- a heavy snoring sound.
A person employed in the loading and unloading of ships' cargoes. Stow in a ship's hold. Load or unload the cargo of a ship.
(also strasser) Trouser.
Persuasion; an instance of this. suasible. suasive. E17. suasory. E17.
Sweet-smelling.
Dark or dusky color, gloom. Also, formal academic dress (dark in color) as worn at some universities. (noun) Dark, dusky, dull, gloomy, sombre, subdued. (adj.)

A minute whitish vesicle or blister caused by sweat collecting in the upper layers of the skin after copious perspiration, esp. in certain fevers or after sunburn. (usu. pl. sudamina) sudoral- pertaining to sweating, esp. a disturbance in the function of sweating. (sudoriferous) sudorific- diaphoretic; promoting sweating.
Uniformly or evenly distributed or spread; even. Smooth.
Of its own kind; peculiar; unique.
In excess of the usual, proper, or prescribed number; additional; extra. Esp. an official or employee engaged only in case of emergency, or an actor w/o speaking part.
Form or cause to form pus. From pus; become converted into and discharge pus.
Bringing something to an end; coming to an end; cessation, esp. temporary; respite. Leave off; stop; forbear; to die; discontinue.
Excess, superfluity; an excessive amount (of) something, esp. food.
Sigh, long (obs. gasp) (at/for). Utter with a sigh. Also: breathe out. Breathe in.
A young man attending a knight; a man servant or attendant. A (young) man. A country laborer; a rustic; a shepherd. A suitor; a male lover or suitor.
The skin of the body, esp. the rind of pork or bacon. The surface of ground grown with grass; turf. A stretch of grassy turf. Ground covered with short, lawn; a garden.
Characterized by or devoted to excessive self-indulgence or luxury; excessively luxurious.
A form of reasoning in which a conclusion is deduced from two given or assumed propositions (premises); a common or middle type that is absent from the conclusion. All A are B. Therefore all B are C.
A race of elemental beings or spirits of the air, orig. in the system of Paracelsus. A slender, graceful woman or girl. A type of hummingbird.
Of, pertaining to, situated in, or characteristic of a wood or woods. Having characteristics of a wood or forest, as tree or shrub; living in a wood.
Orig. a meeting for Christian worship; esp. the Eucharist. Also, the series of prescribed psalms etc. which forms the first part of a liturgy.

Swooning; temporary loss of consciousness caused by an insufficient flow of blood to the brain. (Ling.) the shortening of a word by omission of one or more syllables or letters in the middle, e.g. ne'er. Cut short; reduce.
A government officer, having different powers in different countries; an officer of law; a magistrate. A business agent for a corporation or university; a member of a committee of the senate.

In prosody, a combination of two different feet in a measure; a dipody. A pair of connected or corresponding things. Astron., the conjunction or opposition of the moon with the sun. That which is combined; a pair or couple.
A drum. Later, spec. a small drum, used esp. to accompany a fife or trumpet; a taborist. To play or beat on or as on a tabor; drum.
A low backless seat or stool for one person. A small table, esp. one used as a stand for houseplants; a bedside table.

A small bone in the foot, articulating with the tibia to form the ankle joint (also astragalus). A slope; spec. the sloping side of a wall or earthwork. A scree slope, consisting of material which has fallen from the face of the cliff above. A mountain, hill or iceberg's slope.
At full gallop; swiftly, headlong.
A small mountain lake.
A greyish wild horse of eastern Europe and western Asia, extinct since 1919.

An abyss below Hades where the Titans were confined; a place of punishment in Hades; Hell. A hellish or horrific place or situation. Tartar: central Asian peoples, inc. Mongols and Turks, who under Genghis Khan overran much of Asia and Europe and later controlled central Russia.
Of an orange-brown or yellow-brown color; earlier, any of several shades of brown. A black or dark-skinned person (derog.).

Orig. (now rare), the branch of philosophy that deals with ends or final causes. Later, the belief that nature shows signs of divine or cosmic design or purpose. Now also, the belief or theory that certain phenomena or acts are to be explained in terms of purpose or intention; explanation in such terms; (evidence of) purposiveness in nature.

Comply temporarily with the requirements of a particular time or occasion; avoid committing oneself so as to gain time; procrastinate; employ delaying tactics, esp. in dealing with a person or thing. (BUY TIME)
Having an underlying purpose; (of writing etc.) composed with the intention of promoting a particular cause or viewpoint.
Full of darkness; dark; obscure; gloomy.
A projection on the end or side of a piece of wood or other material, made to fit a mortise (a corresponding cavity) in another piece (tenon and mortise).

Termagant: a god imagined in medieval Christendom to be worshipped esp. by Muslims and represented in mystery plays as a violent overbearing personage (archaic). A violent, overbearing, or quarrelsome woman. Termagancy = termagant quality; violent temper.

Of or pertaining to this world; earthly; worldly; secular; mundane; not heavenly or spiritual. Of the nature of earth; earthy, esp. occurring on or inhabiting dry land. Of or pertaining to the planet Earth.
The vindication of divine providence in relation to the existence of evil; an instance of this; a doctrine etc. in support of this. Optimism.

(From theomachia) A striving or warring against God; opposition to the will of God. A battle or strife among the gods; esp. in reference to that narrated in the Iliad. Theomachist — one who fights against God.
A song of lamentation, esp. for the dead; a dirge.

An old variety of backgammon, played on a board with holes along the edge, in which pegs were placed for scoring. An imitation of a reduplicated or alternating ticking sound such as a clock, or small artillery. A contrivance that makes noise as a practical joke. A system of telegraphy used by bookmakers at race meetings.
A short cape or stole worn around the neck and shoulders. A structure on an animal resembling a tippet. A length of twisted hair or gut to which a fishing hook is attached.
(Also tyro) A beginner, a learner, a novice. From Latin — a young soldier or recruit.
A signal, esp. an alarm-signal, sounded by ringing a bell or bells. A bell used to sound an alarm.

The action or process of clipping the hair or shaving the head; the state of being shorn. The shaving of the head or part of it as a religious practice or rite, esp. as a preparation to entering the clergy or a religious order. The part of a monk's or priest's head left bare by shaving the hair.

Either of two small sharks. A grove or plantation of trees in India. An Indian mound or barrow, esp. the ruins of an ancient stupa. Incline or fall to one side; topple over. Drink (alcohol) in large quantities, esp. habitually.
A place-name, esp. a descriptive one, usually derived from a topographical feature of the place. Any name, as a personal name, etc., derived from a place-name.
Variant of torque.
Inactive, apathetic; slow, sluggish; dull. (Of a part of the body) numb; dormant (of an animal).
The first Grand Inquisitor of Spain (1420–1498).
Scorched, burned; intensely hot, scorching. Ardent, zealous; fiercely passionate.
The seasonal transfer of grazing animals to different pasture, often over long distances. Transhumant — migrating between regions with differing climates.
Leaping or passing from one thing or condition to another; passing abruptly into another.
Cause light to pass through. In medicine, to shine strong light or other radiation through an organ or part to detect disease or abnormality.
Living, originating, or situated beyond, or on the other side of, a range of mountains. Across or over the mountains.
Characterized or affected by trembling. Fearful, timid, vacillating. Ready to vibrate in response to an influence; tremblingly sensitive or responsive to. Writing produced by a tremulous hand.
Cutting, adapted for cutting; having a sharp edge. Of language, style, etc.: incisive, vigorous, clear, effective, energetic. Sharply defined; clear-cut.
A feeder, an eater of a specified kind (stout trencherman, etc.); a person with a hearty appetite. A person who cadges free meals; a parasite. (rare)
An allowance (usu. 4 lbs in 104 lbs) formerly made to purchasers of various goods sold by weight, to compensate for waste during transportation.

Close-fitting trousers or breeches combined with stockings, formerly worn by Irishmen and Scottish Highlanders; a kind of tartan trouser worn by certain Scottish regiments. Close-fitting tartan trousers worn by women.
A Roman couch, running around three sides of a table, on which to recline at meals. Also, a dining room.
In the Middle Ages, the lower division of a university course of study, comprising grammar, rhetoric, and logic. The three anterior ambulacra of an echinoderm.
A foot in prosody, consisting of one long followed by one short syllable, or one stressed followed by one unstressed syllable. Trochaic (adj).
Use of a word or phrase in a sense other than that which is appropriate to it; a figurative or metaphorical use of a word or phrase. An argument advanced by a sceptic.
Characterized by or exhibiting ferocity or aggressiveness; fierce, savage; pugnacious, aggressive, hostile, rude, scathing.
A prostitute, a disreputable or promiscuous woman.
A worthless, useless or trifling article; religious practices, showy clothing, or worthless finery regarded as superficial trappings or superstitious nonsense.
A fine soft silk bobbin-net used for women's dresses, veils, etc. Tulle gras (French): a gauze dressing for the skin impregnated with petroleum jelly.
A ruined Roman city in the Alban Hills, in the Latium region of Italy.

The amount of wine, etc. by which a cask or bottle falls short of being full after leakage, evaporation, or use. The capacity of the part of a vehicle's fuel tank not filled with fuel. Ullagone: a cry of lamentation; a wail.

Beyond what is immediate or present; coming later; further, future. Beyond what is openly stated or evident; intentionally concealed or kept in the background. Situated beyond a point or boundary; more remote in position.
An inflorescence (arrangement of a plant's flowers), often flat-topped, whose stalks or rays all spring from a common center, like the spokes of an umbrella.

Shade, shadow; the shadow of the pointer on a sundial; a reflection. (Archaic) A red-brown earth, darker than ochre and sienna, used to make various pigments; dark brown, dark, dusky. To shade or protect.

A female water-spirit; a nymph (also ondine). A small bulbous flask with a tapered spout, used to irrigate the eye. Undinism: the arousal of sexual thoughts by water, esp. urine and urination; urolagnia.
Of or pertaining to a bear or bears; characteristic of or resembling (that of) a bear; bearlike, bearish.
Sting, prick, prickle; irritate, nettle. Beat with nettles; flagellate.
Greatly or excessively fond of one's wife; doting. Behavior marked by such fondness. (-ly, -ness)
In full vagus nerve. Either of the tenth pair of cranial nerves, which supply the upper digestive tract and the organs of the chest cavity and abdomen.
An oration or farewell address; spoken or delivered on taking farewell.

Any of various plants with small tubular, mostly white or pink flowers, with strong-smelling roots. The chief source of the drug valerian; a bitter-tasting drug used as a sedative and anti-spasmodic. Found in the Mediterranean.
Diversify; give variety to; enliven with differences or changes. Make varied in color or appearance; mark with irregular patches or streaks of different colors or appearance. (-ed, -tion, -tor)

An edition, esp. of the complete works of a classical author, containing the notes of various commentators or editors, or variant readings from manuscripts or earlier editions. (also variorum edition) Variation; (a) novelty; a source of variety. Also, an unnecessary decoration or flourish.
A person able to be bribed; subject to mercenary or corrupt influences. Put on sale or available for purchase. (-ly, -ness, -ity)
Hunter, huntsman. Venatic: of, pertaining to, or used in the hunting of animals. Venation: the action or occupation of hunting animals. The arrangement of veins in plant leaves or insects' wings.
Pale green or bright blue used as a pigment. Basic copper carbonate, formed esp. by atmospheric corrosion as a greenish or bluish patina or incrustation on exposed copper, brass, and bronze; aerugo.
A kind of short wooden or wax match, from Vesta, Roman goddess of the hearth and household.
Of a virgin; serving the goddess Vesta as a priestess. A chaste woman; virgin.
An article of clothing; a garment; clothing, dress; a covering. Now poet. In law, all the vegetation growing on or covering land except trees; a product of land, as grass or corn. Now rare.

Of or pertaining to travel or motion. (Also viaticum) The Eucharist as administered to a person near or in danger of death. Also a supply or official allowance of money for a journey; travelling expenses; a supply of food for a journey.

The fact or liability of change occurring in a specified thing or area; an instance of this. Change or mutability regarded as a natural process or tendency in human affairs. pl. — Changes in circumstances, uncertainties or variations of fortune or outcome.

Woman. Only in biblical allusions with ref. to the name given by Adam to Eve. A woman of masculine strength or spirit; a female warrior; an Amazon. A man of exceptional strength or spirit (rare — Shakes.). A domineering woman; a fierce or abusive woman.
In England, a former measure of land, varying in extent and averaging thirty acres. A rod or pole used as a measure. Of a stem or branch: wand-shaped, long, straight, and slender.
A bright bluish-green chromium oxide color or pigment.

Make incomplete, imperfect, or faulty; mar or spoil the quality of. Contaminate the substance of; make bad, impure, or defective; esp. make air polluted and unfit for breathing. Invalidate; make ineffectual; spec. destroy or impair the legal validity or force of.
The state or character of being guilty of or devoted to vice or immorality. A defect, fault, or imperfection.
A glass display case.
A spiral part or object; a convolution. A spiral scroll characteristic of Ionic capitals and also used in Corinthian and composite capitals. Voluted (adj.) — having the form of a volute.
A member of a people of Gaulish origin inhabiting southern and eastern Belgium and neighboring parts of France. The French dialect spoken by these people.

A salutation or toast when drinking a cup of wine; spiced ale or mulled wine drunk in a toast, esp. on Twelfth Night and Christmas Eve, and New Year's Eve. The custom of caroling house to house at Christmas time, etc. A drinking bout; riotous festivity; revelling, etc.
Widthwise and lengthwise, respectively, threads of the weave of any woven item.

A living being; a creature. A supernatural being. A human being; a person. A certain (esp. small) amount. Usu. in negative contexts. Strong and courageous, esp. in warfare; valiant. Strong, robust, mighty, active, energetic; swift.
A sheet in which to wrap a corpse for burial; a shroud. A mass of solidified wax clinging to the side of a candle, likened to a sheet folded in creases and regarded as a bad omen.
A row of mown grass or hay, sheaves of corn, peats, etc., laid out to be dried by exposure to the wind, etc. To lay or set in windrows.
The European bison.
Overwhelmed or afflicted with misfortune, distress, sorrow, or grief. Exhibiting a state of distress, misery, or grief; sad, miserable, or dismal in appearance.
Having or designating yellow or yellowish hair and a light complexion.

A servant or attendant in a royal or noble household, typically ranking between a sergeant and a groom or between a squire and a page; an officer of a specified department or function (usu. with following designation of office). An assistant to an official, esp. in the navy.
Vagina (Sanskrit).
